questions.explanation: Without polar functional groups and with weak London forces, C–H and C–C bonds require significant energy to break; typical reactions are limited to combustion or, under UV light, substitution with halogens.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Calculate the molar mass of octane, C8H18.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many grams of ethane (C2H6, molar mass 30.07 g/mol) are required to obtain 2.00 moles?
questions.explanation: Mass = moles × molar mass; m = 2.00 mol × 30.07 g/mol = 60.14 g. Final unit: grams (g).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the trend in boiling points of straight-chain alkanes as the carbon chain length increases?
choices: A. Boiling points decrease as chain length increases.
B. Boiling points stay roughly constant.
C. Boiling points increase as chain length increases.
questions.correct_answer: C. Boiling points increase as chain length increases.
questions.explanation: Longer carbon chains have stronger van der Waals forces, leading to higher boiling points as chain length increases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: What is the IUPAC name for the straight-chain alkane with 5 carbons?
questions.explanation: Five-carbon straight chain corresponds to pentane in IUPAC nomenclature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An alkane with 6 carbon atoms has the formula C6H14. Determine its approximate molar mass in g/mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which statement about cycloalkanes is true?
choices: B. They have the general formula CnH2n.
C. They always have higher boiling points than open-chain alkanes with the same carbon count.
D. They have more hydrogens than open-chain alkanes.
questions.correct_answer: B. They have the general formula CnH2n.
questions.explanation: Cycloalkanes are saturated ring compounds with the formula CnH2n, unlike open-chain alkanes (CnH2n+2).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: What is the general formula for saturated acyclic alkanes?
questions.explanation: Acyclic saturated alkanes follow the formula CnH2n+2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the free-radical chlorination of alkanes under UV light, which step is the chain-propagating step that forms the alkyl radical?
questions.explanation: Propagation steps involve the formation and consumption of radicals that propagate the chain reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Cycloalkanes have the general formula CnH2n+2.
questions.explanation: Cycloalkanes have the formula CnH2n, not CnH2n+2; alkenes have CnH2n.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Name two natural sources of hydrocarbons.
questions.explanation: Two major natural hydrocarbon sources listed in Unit 6: natural gas and crude oil.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: State the general formulas for open-chain alkanes and cycloalkanes.
questions.explanation: Open-chain alkanes follow CnH2n+2 while cycloalkanes follow CnH2n.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A natural gas sample contains 60% methane (CH4), 25% ethane (C2H6), and 15% propane (C3H8) by mole. Calculate the mean molar mass of the gas in g/mol.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which of the following physical quantities is a vector?
questions.explanation: Vectors require both magnitude and direction; velocity specifies both.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a vector diagram, what does the length of the drawn arrow represent?
questions.explanation: The arrow length is proportional to the vector's magnitude.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: When adding two vectors graphically, what is the standard head-to-tail method?
choices: Place the tail of the second at the head of the first
questions.correct_answer: Place the tail of the second at the head of the first
questions.explanation: The resultant is drawn from the tail of the first to the head of the second.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two perpendicular vectors have magnitudes 3 N east and 4 N north. The resultant magnitude is?
questions.explanation: Resultant magnitude is sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A vector of magnitude 6 N is directed at 60 degrees above the +x axis. Which of the following are its components?
questions.explanation: Fx = r cos theta, Fy = r sin theta; with r=6, theta=60°

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A vector is completely specified by its magnitude only.
questions.explanation: A vector requires both magnitude and direction for complete description.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What is a unit vector and how is it used when resolving a vector into components?
questions.correct_answer: A unit vector is a vector with magnitude 1 that points in a given direction. It is used to express a vector as a sum of its components along the coordinate axes, e.g., F = Fx î + Fy ĵ, where Fx = |F| cos(theta) and Fy = |F| sin(theta).
questions.explanation: Unit vectors provide direction along axes to separate a vector into components.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: List the basic steps of the graphical method of vector addition.
questions.correct_answer: 1) Choose a scale and mark it. 2) Draw each vector tail-to-head in sequence. 3) Draw the resultant from the starting tail to the final head. 4) Measure the resultant’s magnitude and direction.
questions.explanation: Steps follow the tail-to-head construction; scale ensures accurate representation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A displacement vector has magnitude 12 m at 30 degrees north of east. Find its x and y components. Use +x east, +y north.
questions.explanation: Fx = r cos(theta) = 12 cos(30°) ≈ 10.39 m; Fy = r sin(theta) = 12 sin(30°) = 6.00 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two vectors A = 8 N at 45° and B = 5 N at 135°. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant R.
questions.explanation: Resolve into components: Ax=8cos45≈5.66, Ay=8sin45≈5.66; Bx=5cos135≈-3.54, By=5sin135≈3.54; Rx≈2.12, Ry≈9.19; |R|≈√(Rx^2+Ry^2)≈9.43; θ=atan(Ry/Rx)≈77°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Vectors have both magnitude and direction; displacement specifies a change in position with a direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which notation represents a vector quantity algebraically?
choices: A bold letter such as A or an arrow over A
questions.correct_answer: A bold letter such as A or an arrow over A
questions.explanation: Vectors are represented by a bold letter or an arrow over the letter to indicate direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: If vector A is 3 m east and vector B is 4 m north, their resultant has magnitude and direction approximately:
questions.explanation: Resultant magnitude is sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5 m; angle tanθ = 4/3 ⇒ θ ≈ 53.1° north of east.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which method is used to add two vectors graphically?
questions.explanation: Graphical addition is often performed using the parallelogram law (head-to-tail approach).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A vector A has magnitude 10 N at 60° above the +x axis. Its x- and y-components are:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A scalar quantity has both magnitude and direction.
questions.explanation: Scalar quantities have magnitude only; vectors have both magnitude and direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Give two examples of vector quantities and two examples of scalar quantities.
questions.correct_answer: Vector: displacement, velocity; Scalar: mass, temperature
questions.explanation: Vectors require magnitude and direction; scalars require only magnitude and unit.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Briefly outline the steps to add two vectors using the head-to-tail (parallelogram) method.
questions.correct_answer: Draw both vectors from a common starting point; place the tail of one at the head of the other (head-to-tail); draw the resultant as the diagonal of the parallelogram; measure magnitude and direction using the chosen scale.
questions.explanation: Head-to-tail method is the graphical approach for vector addition.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A force of 9 N is applied at 40° above the +x axis. Find the x- and y-components (to 2 decimals) and provide the final units.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Resolve a force of 12 N acting at 60° above the +x axis into x- and y-components.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which of the following quantities is a vector?
questions.explanation: A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction. Mass, distance, and temperature are scalars with magnitude only.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a vector diagram drawn to scale, what does the length of the arrow represent?
questions.explanation: In vector diagrams, the length is proportional to the vector's magnitude; direction is shown by the arrowhead.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which operation corresponds to placing vectors head-to-tail to obtain the resultant?
questions.explanation: Adding vectors by the head-to-tail method yields the resultant vector.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Resolving a vector into horizontal and vertical components uses which axes?
questions.explanation: Resolving a vector uses horizontal and vertical (x and y) components along the chosen axes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two equal vectors of 6 N each act with an angle of 60 degrees between them. What is the magnitude of the resultant?
questions.explanation: R = sqrt(A^2 + A^2 + 2A^2 cosθ) with A=6, θ=60 gives R = 6√3 ≈ 10.39 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Displacement and distance are the same when motion is in a straight line with constant direction.
questions.explanation: When motion is along a straight line with no direction change, net displacement equals distance travelled.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Name two scalar quantities and two vector quantities.
questions.correct_answer: Scalar: mass, temperature; Vector: velocity, force
questions.explanation: Scalar quantities have only magnitude; vector quantities have magnitude and direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Resolve the 70 N force directed 150° from the +x axis into its x and y components.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two vectors: A = 30 N directed east; B = 40 N at 60° north of east. Find the resultant magnitude and direction (from +x).
questions.correct_answer: R ≈ 60.8 N at ≈ 34.7° north of east
questions.explanation: Decompose B into components: Bx=40 cos60=20; By=40 sin60≈34.64; R components: Rx=50, Ry=34.64; magnitude ≈ sqrt(50^2+34.64^2) ≈ 60.8 N; direction arctan(34.64/50) ≈ 34.7° north of east.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Resolve a 40 N force acting at 30° above the +x axis into its horizontal (x) and vertical (y) components.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which of the following quantities is a vector? (Distinct application example 31.)
questions.explanation: A vector has both magnitude and direction; temperature, mass, and time are scalars.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes vector notation?
choices: A bold letter denotes a vector quantity or an arrow over the letter indicates a vector; |S| denotes a scalar magnitude.
An arrow over a letter denotes a scalar value.
A bold letter always denotes a scalar quantity.
A vector has no magnitude, only direction.
questions.correct_answer: A bold letter denotes a vector quantity or an arrow over the letter indicates a vector; |S| denotes a scalar magnitude.
questions.explanation: Vectors can be represented by bold letters or with an arrow; |S| gives only magnitude.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A vector diagram is primarily used to show:
choices: Only the magnitude of a vector
Only the direction of a vector
Both magnitude and direction with an arrow representing the vector
The position of the vector's tail at the origin
questions.correct_answer: Both magnitude and direction with an arrow representing the vector
questions.explanation: Vectors are shown with arrows where length indicates magnitude and direction indicates orientation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which method is used to add two vectors graphically? (Distinct application example 34.)
questions.explanation: Graphical addition places the tail of the second vector at the head of the first; the resulting vector is from tail to head of the two vectors.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which statement is true about resolving a vector into components?
choices: A vector has only horizontal components
A vector can be resolved into horizontal and vertical components using trigonometric projections
Components are always equal in magnitude
Components do not depend on the angle of the vector
questions.correct_answer: A vector can be resolved into horizontal and vertical components using trigonometric projections
questions.explanation: Components depend on the angle; use cos for horizontal, sin for vertical (assuming angle from x-axis).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Scalars require both magnitude and direction for a complete description.
questions.explanation: Scalar quantities have magnitude only; direction is not required for a complete description.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Explain how to resolve a force of 5 N at 30° north of east into horizontal and vertical components.
questions.correct_answer: Fx = 5 cos 30° ≈ 4.33 N (east); Fy = 5 sin 30° ≈ 2.50 N (north). The components are found using F cosθ for horizontal and F sinθ for vertical, with angles measured from the +x axis (east).
questions.explanation: Use standard component resolution: Fx = F cosθ, Fy = F sinθ.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A boat travels 6.0 km at 20° north of east, then 8.0 km at 60° north of east. Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant displacement.
questions.correct_answer: Resultant displacement: components: x = 6 cos20 + 8 cos60 = 5.638 + 4.000 = 9.638 km; y = 6 sin20 + 8 sin60 = 2.052 + 6.928 = 8.980 km. Magnitude ≈ 13.2 km; direction ≈ arctan(8.980/9.638) ≈ 43.6° north of east.
questions.explanation: Use vector components and Pythagoras to obtain resultant magnitude and arctan for direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two displacement vectors A and B have magnitudes 5.0 m and 7.0 m and are at an angle of 40° to each other. What is the magnitude of their resultant displacement? Provide all values, units, and context.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Resolve a displacement vector of magnitude 12.0 m directed 25° north of west into its x (horizontal) and y (vertical) components. Provide the components with correct signs and units.
questions.explanation: Vx = 12 cos25° toward west (negative x); Vy = 12 sin25° toward north (positive y).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s^2 for 5 s. What is the displacement during this interval?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Displacement is best described as:
choices: a) the total distance travelled along the path
b) final position minus initial position
c) the average speed over the interval
d) the magnitude of the velocity vector
questions.correct_answer: b) final position minus initial position
questions.explanation: Displacement is a vector describing the straight-line change in position from the initial to the final point, not the path length.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A particle’s position is given by s = 2t^2 + 3 (m). What is the average velocity from t = 0 to t = 5 s?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: On a velocity-time graph that rises linearly from 0 to 20 m/s over 4 s, what is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the slope of the v–t graph: a = Δv/Δt = (20 − 0)/4 = 5 m/s^2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A car starts from a speed of 4 m/s and accelerates at 3 m/s^2 for 6 s. It then continues at a constant speed for 4 s. What is the total displacement in 10 s?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The instantaneous velocity is the slope of the position-time graph.
questions.explanation: The instantaneous velocity at a specific time is given by the slope of the position-time graph at that time.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Define acceleration.
questions.correct_answer: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
questions.explanation: Acceleration describes how velocity changes per unit time (a = Δv/Δt).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What does the slope of a velocity-time graph represent?
questions.explanation: The slope of the velocity-time graph corresponds to the acceleration (for constant acceleration).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 3 m/s^2 for 5 s, then decelerates at -2 m/s^2 for 4 s. What is the final velocity after the 9 s, and the total displacement during those 9 s? Provide the numerical values with units.
questions.correct_answer: Final velocity: 7 m/s; Total displacement: 81.5 m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A particle starts with velocity 12 m/s and accelerates uniformly at 0.5 m/s^2 for 10 s. What is the displacement during the 10 s? Provide the numerical answer with units and brief method.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A car increases its velocity from 0 to 20 m/s in 4 s. What is its average acceleration?
questions.explanation: Average acceleration a_avg = Δv/Δt = (20 − 0)/4 = 5 m/s^2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A ball starts from rest and accelerates at 2 m/s^2 for 3 s. How far does it travel in that time?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a velocity-time graph for an object with constant acceleration, what does the slope represent?
questions.explanation: For constant acceleration, a is the slope of v vs t.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A car starts at 5 m/s and accelerates at 1 m/s^2 for 6 s. Its final velocity is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An object with initial speed u = 4 m/s accelerates at a = 2 m/s^2. It covers a displacement of s = 80 m in a straight line. What is the time t required? Use s = ut + 0.5 a t^2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: If velocity changes uniformly with time, acceleration is constant.
questions.explanation: Uniform rate of velocity change implies constant acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Explain the difference between average velocity and instantaneous velocity.
questions.correct_answer: Average velocity is displacement divided by the time interval; instantaneous velocity is the velocity at a specific instant (the limit as the time interval approaches zero).
questions.explanation: Average velocity uses a finite time interval; instantaneous velocity is the velocity at a single moment.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Describe how the displacement relates to the area under a velocity-time graph for motion with changing velocity.
questions.correct_answer: Displacement equals the area under the velocity-time graph; positive area corresponds to forward motion, negative area to backward motion.
questions.explanation: Area under v-t graph represents net displacement during the time interval.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A car starts from rest (u = 0) and accelerates at a = 1.5 m/s^2 for t = 8 s. What distance does it cover? Provide all values, units, method, final unit.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An object with initial velocity u = 4 m/s accelerates at a = 2 m/s^2. It covers a displacement s = 80 m in a straight line. Find the time t required.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 3 m/s^2 for 4 s. What is its final velocity?
questions.explanation: Using v = u + at with u = 0, a = 3 m/s^2, t = 4 s; v = 0 + 3×4 = 12 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about constant acceleration is true?
choices: The velocity changes at a constant rate
The velocity is zero at all times
questions.correct_answer: The velocity changes at a constant rate
questions.explanation: Constant acceleration means the rate of change of velocity is constant; velocity changes at a constant rate.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The velocity–time graph of an object with constant acceleration is a straight line.
questions.explanation: With constant acceleration, velocity changes linearly with time, producing a straight-line v-t graph.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which equation gives the displacement s after time t for an object with initial velocity u and constant acceleration a?
questions.explanation: For constant acceleration, displacement s = ut + (1/2) a t^2 is the standard equation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An object starts from speed u = -5 m/s and accelerates at a = 3 m/s^2 for t = 4 s. What is the displacement s during this interval?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Define average velocity and instantaneous velocity, and explain how they differ.
questions.correct_answer: Average velocity is total displacement divided by total time; instantaneous velocity is the velocity at a specific time, equal to the slope of the position-time graph at that time.
questions.explanation: Average velocity uses overall displacement/time; instantaneous velocity uses the slope at a specific moment on a position-time graph.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A particle starts from u = 10 m/s and accelerates uniformly at a = -2 m/s^2 for t = 6 s. Find the displacement s in this interval. Provide your answer with units.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A car moves east with initial speed u = 15 m/s and experiences a constant westward acceleration a = -3 m/s^2 for t = 6 s. What is the displacement s during this interval? Provide your answer with units.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Explain how instantaneous velocity is determined from a position-time graph and how it relates to average velocity.
questions.correct_answer: Instantaneous velocity is the slope of the position-time graph at a single time; average velocity is the total displacement divided by the total time.
questions.explanation: The slope at a single time gives instantaneous velocity; average velocity uses whole interval.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The displacement–time graph for an object undergoing uniform acceleration is which of the following, and what does the slope represent?
choices: A straight line; slope represents velocity
A straight line; slope represents acceleration
questions.explanation: The displacement-time (s-t) graph for uniform acceleration is a parabola; the slope at any time is the instantaneous velocity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In one dimension, displacement is:
choices: A) the distance travelled along the path
B) the final position minus the initial position without direction
C) the straight-line difference between final and initial positions with direction
D) the rate of change of velocity
questions.correct_answer: A) the distance travelled along the path
questions.explanation: Displacement is the vector from the initial to the final position, including direction; it equals the change in position x2−x1 along the straight line joining the points.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A car speeds up from v = 0 to v = 20 m/s in 4 seconds with constant acceleration. What is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration a = Δv/Δt = (20 − 0) / 4 = 5 m/s^2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which equation would you use to relate displacement s, initial velocity u, acceleration a, and time t to find velocity after time t?
choices: B) s = u t + 1/2 a t^2
questions.explanation: In constant acceleration, velocity after time t is v = u + a t.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: On a velocity-time graph for uniformly accelerated motion, the area under the curve between t1 and t2 represents:
questions.explanation: The area under a velocity-time graph over a time interval equals the displacement during that interval.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two trains move in the same direction with speeds 20 m/s and 15 m/s. The relative speed of the second with respect to the first is:
questions.explanation: Relative speed is the difference of speeds when moving in the same direction: 20 − 15 = 5 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The equation s = u t + 1/2 a t^2 is valid for any motion.
questions.explanation: That equation is valid only for motion with constant acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Explain what instantaneous velocity means and how it differs from average velocity.
questions.correct_answer: Instantaneous velocity is the velocity at a specific instant in time (the slope of the position-time curve at that instant). It can differ from the average velocity, which is the total displacement over a time interval divided by the length of that interval. In uniformly accelerated motion, instantaneous velocity changes with time, while average velocity over an interval equals the average of the initial and final velocities over that interval.
questions.explanation: Instantaneous velocity = v(t0); average velocity over [t1,t2] = (v1 + v2)/2 for constant acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Describe how the slope and the area on a velocity-time graph relate to acceleration and displacement in uniformly accelerated motion.
questions.correct_answer: The slope of the velocity-time graph gives acceleration; the area under the velocity-time graph over a time interval gives displacement.
questions.explanation: For v(t) = u + at, slope = a; area under v(t) from t1 to t2 = ∫ v dt = displacement.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A cart starts with velocity 5 m/s and accelerates at 2 m/s^2 for 4 s. Find its final velocity and displacement.
questions.explanation: Final velocity: v = u + a t = 5 + 2×4 = 13 m/s. Displacement: s = ut + 1/2 a t^2 = 5×4 + 1/2×2×16 = 20 + 16 = 36 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A car accelerates at 2 m/s^2 for 5 s, then coasts (a = 0) for 3 s. Find the total displacement in the first 8 s.
questions.explanation: First 5 s: s1 = ut + 1/2 a t^2 = 0 + 1/2×2×25 = 25 m; velocity after 5 s: v1 = 0 + 2×5 = 10 m/s. Next 3 s: s2 = v1 × 3 = 10 × 3 = 30 m. Total s = 25 + 30 = 55 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: A simply supported beam AB of length 3.0 m carries a downward load W = 90 N acting at its midpoint and an additional downward point load P = 20 N located 0.5 m from the left end A. The beam is supported at A and B. Which of the following gives the correct reaction forces at the supports A and B?
questions.explanation: Sum of vertical forces: RA+RB = 110 N. Moments about A: RB*3.0 = 90*1.5 + 20*0.5 = 145 → RB ≈ 48.3 N. Then RA ≈ 61.7 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: In static equilibrium, the sum of moments about any point on the body is zero.
questions.explanation: For equilibrium, both the resultant force and the resultant moment must be zero; thus the moments about any chosen point sum to zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Which statement best distinguishes elastic deformation from plastic deformation?
choices: Elastic deformation is permanent; plastic deformation is recoverable.
Elastic deformation is recoverable after removing the load; plastic deformation is permanent.
Both are always reversible regardless of load history.
Only plastic deformation occurs under tensile loading.
questions.correct_answer: Elastic deformation is recoverable after removing the load; plastic deformation is permanent.
questions.explanation: In elasticity, materials return to original shape after unloading; plastic deformation leaves permanent shape change.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Which statement correctly defines the Young's modulus of a material in the elastic region?
choices: It is the ratio of strain to stress.
It is the ratio of stress to strain in the elastic limit.
It is the product of stress and strain.
It is the sum of stress and strain.
questions.correct_answer: It is the ratio of stress to strain in the elastic limit.
questions.explanation: Young's modulus E = σ/ε in the elastic region; measures stiffness.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: State the SI unit of density and briefly explain what it represents.
questions.explanation: Density is mass per unit volume; the SI unit is kilograms per cubic meter (kg/m^3).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Describe the difference between stress and strain.
questions.correct_answer: Stress is force per unit area; strain is the fractional change in dimension (deformation) of a body.
questions.explanation: Stress (σ) is the internal force per area; strain (ε) is the relative deformation ΔL/L or similar measures.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: A simply supported beam AB of length 5.0 m is supported at A and B. A downward load W = 150 N acts at the midspan (2.5 m from A). A further downward load P = 60 N acts at x = 1.0 m from A. Calculate the reactions at A and B.
questions.explanation: Sum of forces: RA+RB = 210 N. Moments about A: RB*5.0 = 150*2.5 + 60*1.0 = 435 → RB ≈ 87 N. RA ≈ 210 - 87 = 123 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: A wire of length L = 2.0 m and cross-sectional area A = 1.0×10−4 m^2 is stretched by a force F = 1000 N, producing an extension ΔL = 0.0005 m. Calculate the Young’s modulus E. Provide the method and final unit.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Which statement about the stress-strain curve for a material in the elastic region is true?
choices: A. The slope (stiffness) decreases as strain increases.
B. The stress is independent of strain.
C. Stress is proportional to strain, with a constant slope equal to Young's modulus.
D. The area under the curve is zero.
questions.correct_answer: C. Stress is proportional to strain, with a constant slope equal to Young's modulus.
questions.explanation: In the elastic region, Hooke's law holds: σ = Eε; slope equals E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Specific gravity of a substance is defined as the ratio of its density to the density of water at 4°C. What is its unit?
questions.explanation: Specific gravity is a ratio of densities, so the units cancel; SG is dimensionless.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: In static equilibrium of a rigid body, which statement is true?
choices: The resultant of all external forces on the body is zero.
The sum of all external moments on the body is zero.
The velocity of the body is zero at all times.
The potential energy of the body is minimized in every configuration.
questions.correct_answer: The resultant of all external forces on the body is zero.
questions.explanation: This reflects the First Condition of Equilibrium: the net force on the body must be zero for equilibrium, which also implies no linear acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Young's modulus is defined as E = stress divided by strain. Which of the following is the correct statement?
questions.explanation: Young's modulus relates stress and strain in the elastic region: E = σ/ε. The unit is Pascal (Pa).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Elastic limit is defined as the maximum stress that can be applied to a material without causing:
choices: Elastic rebound to a larger shape
questions.explanation: Beyond the elastic limit, permanent (plastic) deformation occurs; within the elastic limit, the material returns to its original shape when the load is removed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: A block has density 7800 kg/m^3 while water has density 1000 kg/m^3. What is its specific gravity (relative to water)?
questions.explanation: Specific gravity is the ratio of the object's density to the density of water (rho_block / rho_water).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: A uniform rod of length 2 m with weight 20 N is hinged at its left end. It is held horizontally by a rope attached to the right end making an angle of 30° above the horizontal. If in equilibrium, what is the tension T in the rope?
questions.explanation: Taking moments about the hinge: T sin(30°) × 2 m = 20 N × 1 m. With sin(30°)=0.5, T × 1 = 20 → T = 20 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: The second condition of equilibrium requires that the sum of moments about any point must be zero.
questions.explanation: The second condition states that the net moment (torque) about any point is zero for equilibrium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Explain briefly what is meant by the first condition of equilibrium and give a simple example from a static, rigid-body situation.
questions.correct_answer: The first condition requires the vector sum of all forces on the body to be zero, so there is no acceleration. Example: a book at rest on a table, where the upward normal force and downward gravitational force are equal and opposite.
questions.explanation: The first condition requires the net force to be zero, so the object has no acceleration. In the textbook example of a book at rest on a table, the upward normal force and downward gravitational force are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, making the net force zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Define strain and describe the difference between tensile and compressive strain.
questions.correct_answer: Strain is the dimensionless fractional change in a body’s length, volume, or geometry caused by stress. Tensile strain is the change in length caused by a longitudinal pulling force; compressive strain is the corresponding shortening under a longitudinal compressing force.
questions.explanation: Strain is the fractional change in length (ΔL/L0) due to applied stress. Tensile strain stretches the material (ΔL>0); compressive strain shortens it (ΔL<0).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: A solid of volume 0.002 m^3 is completely submerged in water. Given water density 1000 kg/m^3 and g = 9.81 m/s^2, calculate the buoyant force on the block. Provide the method and final unit.
questions.correct_answer: Buoyant force F_b = ρ_water × g × V_sub = 1000 × 9.81 × 0.002 = 19.62 N
questions.explanation: Buoyant force equals the weight of the displaced water (Archimedes' principle). Here V_sub = 0.002 m^3, ρ_water = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2; F_b = 19.62 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: A solid block of volume 0.004 m^3 has density 900 kg/m^3. What is its weight? Provide the method and final unit.
questions.explanation: Mass m = density × volume; m = 900 × 0.004 = 3.6 kg. Weight W = m g = 3.6 × 9.81 ≈ 35.3 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: In static equilibrium, the vector sum of all forces acting on a rigid body must be what?
choices: Forces must pass through the same point.
questions.explanation: First condition of equilibrium states that the net force is zero (∑F = 0) for a body to be in equilibrium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Which option correctly defines Young's modulus?
choices: The ratio of longitudinal stress to longitudinal strain in the elastic region.
The ratio of longitudinal strain to longitudinal stress in the elastic region.
Force divided by the cross-sectional area.
Mass divided by the volume of the material.
questions.correct_answer: The ratio of longitudinal stress to longitudinal strain in the elastic region.
questions.explanation: Young's modulus E is defined as stress over strain in the elastic (linear) region.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Which statement about static equilibrium is true?
choices: The resultant force must be zero but moments may be nonzero.
The resultant moment must be zero but forces may be nonzero.
Both the resultant force and the resultant moment must be zero.
Both the resultant force and resultant moment can be nonzero.
questions.correct_answer: The resultant force must be zero but moments may be nonzero.
questions.explanation: A body in static equilibrium has zero net force and zero net moment about any point.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: If a rod is stretched within its elastic limit and the applied force is doubled while the cross-sectional area remains constant, what happens to the Young's modulus (E)?
choices: Doubling the force doubles both stress and strain, leaving E unchanged.
Doubling the force doubles stress but leaves strain unchanged.
Stress remains unchanged and strain doubles.
Doubling both stress and strain would double E.
questions.correct_answer: Doubling the force doubles both stress and strain, leaving E unchanged.
questions.explanation: Within the elastic region, E remains constant for a material; doubling the force increases both stress and strain proportionally, so E stays the same.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: For static equilibrium, the sum of moments (torques) about any point must be zero.
questions.explanation: Second condition of equilibrium requires zero net torque about any point.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Specific gravity of a liquid is
choices: The ratio of the density of the liquid to the density of water at a reference temperature
The mass of water displaced by the liquid
The ratio of pressure to volume of the liquid
questions.correct_answer: The ratio of the density of the liquid to the density of water at a reference temperature
questions.explanation: Specific gravity is density divided by density of water at a reference temperature; it is unitless.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Define elastic deformation and plastic deformation.
questions.correct_answer: Elastic deformation is a reversible deformation that disappears when the load is removed; plastic deformation is permanent, remaining after removing the load (beyond the elastic limit).
questions.explanation: Elastic deformation is recoverable; plastic deformation results in permanent shape change after unloading.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: State the second condition of equilibrium and describe how you would verify it for a rigid body using torque about a chosen point.
questions.correct_answer: The second condition states that the sum of moments (torques) about any axis/point must be zero for equilibrium. To verify, compute the torques of all forces about a chosen point and ensure their algebraic sum is zero; if not, adjust unknowns (e.g., support reactions) until the sum is zero.
questions.explanation: For a body in equilibrium, both the net force and the net moment are zero; torque balance about any point ensures rotational equilibrium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: A steel rod of length L = 2.0 m and cross-sectional area A = 1.0e-4 m^2 is stretched by a force F = 500 N along its length. The measured extension ΔL = 0.0005 m. Calculate Young's modulus E.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: A uniform beam of length 3.0 m and weight 120 N is simply supported at its ends A and B. The weight acts at the midpoint of the beam. Determine the vertical reaction forces at A and at B.
questions.explanation: Take moments about A: RB × 3.0 m = 120 N × 1.5 m → RB = 60 N. Then RA = W − RB = 60 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Which statement describes the first condition of equilibrium for a rigid body in static equilibrium?
choices: A) The net external force on the body is zero.
B) The net external torque about any point is zero.
C) The body must be at rest.
questions.correct_answer: A) The net external force on the body is zero.
questions.explanation: In static equilibrium, the resultant force must be zero; this is the first condition of equilibrium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Young's modulus is defined as
questions.explanation: Young's modulus E = stress/strain; it measures material stiffness.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: A sample with density 900 kg/m^3 has a specific gravity of 0.9. Which of the following represents specific gravity?
questions.explanation: Specific gravity is the ratio of density to density of water (1000 kg/m^3).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: In static equilibrium, which statement is true about torques (moments)?
choices: A) The net force must be zero.
B) The sum of torques about any point must be zero.
C) Both net force and torque must be zero.
D) The body can rotate if the net torque is nonzero.
questions.correct_answer: C) Both net force and torque must be zero.
questions.explanation: The second condition of equilibrium states that the sum of torques about any point must be zero (in addition to net force being zero).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Which statement best describes elastic deformation?
choices: A) It is permanent and cannot be recovered.
B) It is reversible; the material returns to its original shape when the load is removed.
C) It only occurs in plastics and ceramics.
D) It increases with time under constant load.
questions.correct_answer: B) It is reversible; the material returns to its original shape when the load is removed.
questions.explanation: Elastic deformation is reversible; plastic deformation is permanent.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: In static equilibrium, the resultant force must be zero and the resultant torque must also be zero.
questions.explanation: Yes. Both net force and net torque must be zero for static equilibrium of a rigid body.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Describe in one sentence the difference between the first and second conditions of equilibrium.
questions.correct_answer: First condition: net external force is zero; Second condition: sum of moments (torques) about any point is zero.
questions.explanation: The first condition ensures no net force; the second ensures no net rotational effect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: Describe, in two to three sentences, how Young's modulus can be determined experimentally using a wire and measurement of extension under known loads.
questions.correct_answer: Use E = (F/A) / (ΔL/L) = (F L) / (A ΔL); apply a known weight F to a wire with cross-sectional area A and length L, measure extension ΔL, then compute E. The resulting unit is Pa (N/m^2).
questions.explanation: This method uses Hooke's law for a rod; E relates stress and strain.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: A uniform horizontal rod of length 2.0 m weighs 60 N is supported by two vertical ropes at its ends. The left rope has a tension of 30 N. Find the tension in the right rope.
questions.explanation: Sum of vertical forces: T_left + T_right = W; thus T_right = 60 - 30 = 30 N. Taking moments about the left end: T_right * 2.0 m = W * 1.0 m; T_right = 30 N. Both methods yield 30 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.unit_title: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Body
questions.question_text: A horizontal beam 6.0 m long is supported at its ends A and B. A 200 N weight acts at 2.0 m from A. Determine the reactions at supports RA and RB.
questions.explanation: Take moments about A: RB * 6.0 = 200 * 2.0 => RB = 66.7 N. Then RA = 200 - 66.7 = 133.3 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Charge exists in nature as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Charges come in two types: positive and negative; like charges repel, unlike attract.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which method charges a body by rubbing with another material?
questions.explanation: Charging by friction occurs when two insulators rub together, transferring charge.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An electroscope is used to detect what?
questions.explanation: An electroscope detects the presence and magnitude of static charges by leaf divergence.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Electrical discharge through air occurs due to what process?
questions.explanation: Discharge through air happens when air becomes ionized, allowing charge flow.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Ohm's Law relates V, I, and R by V = I R. If R is constant and voltage doubles, what happens to current?
questions.explanation: I = V/R; with R fixed, doubling V doubles I.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Inside a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium, the electric field is zero.
questions.explanation: In electrostatic equilibrium, charges rearrange to cancel internal electric fields.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Where should a voltmeter be connected to measure potential difference across a component?
questions.explanation: A voltmeter measures across the component, so it is connected in parallel.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What is the role of a switch in an electric circuit?
questions.correct_answer: To open or close the circuit, controlling current flow.
questions.explanation: A switch toggles connectivity, turning devices on or off by completing or breaking the circuit.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two point charges q1 = +3 μC and q2 = -5 μC are separated by r = 0.20 m. Calculate the magnitude of the electrostatic force between them. Use k = 8.99×10^9 N m^2/C^2. Show steps and final unit.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A 12 V source is connected to a network where R1 = 6 Ω is in series with the parallel combo of R2 = 3 Ω and R3 = 6 Ω. Find the total current drawn from the source.
questions.explanation: Parallel of 3 Ω and 6 Ω is (3×6)/(3+6) = 2 Ω. Total R = 6 Ω + 2 Ω = 8 Ω. I = V/R = 12/8 = 1.5 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: According to Ohm's law, which statement is true?
choices: A) The current is directly proportional to the voltage for a given resistance.
B) The current is inversely proportional to the voltage for a given resistance.
C) The voltage is independent of resistance.
D) The resistance is independent of temperature.
questions.correct_answer: A) The current is directly proportional to the voltage for a given resistance.
questions.explanation: Ohm's law is V = IR. For a fixed resistance, current I is proportional to voltage V. The other statements misstate the relationships.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The direction of the electric field around a positive point charge is:
choices: C) perpendicular to the radial direction
questions.explanation: Electric field lines emanate outward from a positive charge, showing the field direction away from the charge.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a simple circuit with a battery and a resistor, where should the ammeter be placed to measure current?
choices: A) In parallel with the resistor
B) In series with the resistor
questions.correct_answer: B) In series with the resistor
questions.explanation: An ammeter must be in series with the component whose current you want to measure so that the same current flows through both.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel to a 12 V source. What is their equivalent resistance?
questions.explanation: For parallel resistors, 1/R_eq = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/6 + 2/6 = 3/6 = 1/2, so R_eq = 2 Ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: If you double the distance between two charges, the electrostatic force between them becomes:
questions.explanation: Coulomb's law F ∝ 1/r^2; doubling r makes F decrease by a factor of 4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An ideal voltmeter should be connected in series with the component whose voltage it is measuring.
questions.explanation: A voltmeter should be connected in parallel with the component to measure its voltage without significantly altering the circuit.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: State Ohm's law and define the symbols V, I and R.
questions.correct_answer: Ohm's law states V = IR, where V is the voltage across the element, I is the current through it, and R is the resistance.
questions.explanation: Ohm's law relates voltage, current, and resistance; V is voltage, I is current, R is resistance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Explain how increasing resistance affects current in a circuit with fixed voltage.
questions.correct_answer: Increasing resistance reduces current because I = V/R; for constant V, I decreases as R increases.
questions.explanation: With a fixed voltage, increasing R lowers the current according to Ohm's law.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A 9 V battery is connected across a 3 Ω resistor. What is the current in the circuit? Show your calculation.
questions.explanation: Using Ohm's law I = V/R, I = 9 V / 3 Ω = 3 A. Final unit: amperes (A).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two resistors, 3 Ω and 6 Ω, are in series with a 12 V supply. What is the current in the circuit? Show your calculation.
questions.explanation: Total resistance R = 3 Ω + 6 Ω = 9 Ω. Current I = V / R = 12 V / 9 Ω = 1.33 A (approx).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which method of charging a body involves rubbing two insulating materials together to transfer charge?
questions.explanation: Charging by friction occurs when two insulators are rubbed together, transferring electrons and producing opposite charges on the objects.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Coulomb’s law states that the magnitude of the electrostatic force between two point charges is proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
choices: Only for charges of equal magnitude
questions.explanation: Coulomb’s law: F ∝ |q1 q2| / r^2; the force acts along the line joining the charges.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Electrical discharge through air can occur when a large potential difference ionizes the air, creating a conductive path.
questions.explanation: Discharge happens when air is ionized by a strong electric field creating a conductive path (spark, ionization).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a series circuit, the current through each resistor is the same.
questions.explanation: In a series circuit the same current flows through all components; voltages add up across components.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Where should a voltmeter be connected to measure the potential difference across a resistor?
questions.explanation: Voltmeter has very high resistance and is connected in parallel to the component whose voltage is measured.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two point charges q1=3 μC and q2=-2 μC are separated by r=0.05 m. Using Coulomb’s law, which is the correct magnitude of the electrostatic force (k=9×10^9 N m^2/C^2)?
questions.explanation: F = k|q1 q2|/r^2 = 9e9 × (3e-6 × 2e-6) / (0.05)^2 = 0.054 / 0.0025 = 21.6 N. Direction is attractive since charges have opposite signs.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: State Ohm’s law and identify what each symbol represents.
questions.correct_answer: Ohm's law: V = IR; V is voltage (potential difference), I is current, R is resistance.
questions.explanation: Ohm’s law relates the current through a conductor to the voltage and its resistance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Explain why an ammeter must be connected in series and a voltmeter in parallel in a circuit.
questions.correct_answer: An ammeter is placed in series to measure the current through a component without altering the circuit; a voltmeter is placed in parallel to measure potential difference across a component, while drawing minimal current due to its high resistance.
questions.explanation: Connecting ammeter in series ensures it measures the through-path current; voltmeter in parallel across component measures potential difference without significantly changing current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A resistor of 4 Ω is connected to a 12 V source. Calculate the current flowing through the resistor.
questions.explanation: Using Ohm's law I = V/R, I = 12 V / 4 Ω = 3 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two resistors 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel across a 12 V source. Calculate the equivalent resistance of the parallel combination and the total current supplied by the source.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which method of charging involves transfer of charge by touching two objects together?
questions.explanation: Charging by conduction occurs when electrons are transferred through direct contact between objects.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What causes the leaves of a gold-leaf electroscope to diverge when a charged rod is brought near but not touching?
questions.explanation: The presence of a nearby charged object induces charges on the leaves; like charges repel causing divergence.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: If the distance between two identical charges is doubled, what happens to the electrostatic force between them?
questions.explanation: Coulomb's law states F ∝ 1/r^2; doubling r reduces the force to one quarter.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Electric field strength at a point is defined as the force experienced by a test charge per unit charge.
questions.explanation: E = F/q for a small test charge q; the field strength is the force per unit charge.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a parallel circuit with resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω connected to the same 12 V supply, which resistor carries the largest current?
questions.explanation: In parallel, current in each branch is I = V/R. The smallest resistance draws the largest current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Charging by friction creates new electric charges; charge is not conserved.
questions.explanation: Charge is transferred between bodies; total charge is conserved.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: State Coulomb's law and describe how the force changes when either charge or distance changes.
questions.correct_answer: F = k |q1 q2| / r^2. The force increases with the product of the charges and decreases with the square of the distance.
questions.explanation: Coulomb's law relates the electrostatic force between two point charges to the product of the charges and the inverse square of their separation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What is the direction of the electric field inside a conductor at electrostatic equilibrium?
questions.explanation: In electrostatic equilibrium, charges rearrange so that no net electric field exists inside the conductor.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two resistors of 4 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in series to a 9 V battery. Find the current in the circuit (show steps and final unit).
questions.explanation: R_total = 4 + 6 = 10 Ω; I = V / R_total = 9 V / 10 Ω = 0.9 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω, and 6 Ω are connected in parallel across a 12 V source. Find the equivalent resistance and the total current drawn from the source (show steps and final units).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes a magnet?
choices: A magnet has two poles: North and South.
A magnet loses magnetic properties only when cooled.
All magnets are temporary and lose magnetism easily.
questions.correct_answer: A magnet has two poles: North and South.
questions.explanation: Magnets inherently have two poles, North and South. Like poles attract and unlike poles repel. Magnets can attract iron or steel, and they can be permanent, temporary, or electromagnets.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which statement about magnetic field lines around a bar magnet is true?
choices: Field lines form open curves that end at infinity.
Field lines exit the magnet at the North end and enter at the South end.
Field lines only exist outside the magnet.
Field lines are straight lines radiating out from the magnet.
questions.correct_answer: Field lines exit the magnet at the North end and enter at the South end.
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines emerge from the North pole of a magnet and curve around to enter the South pole, forming a pattern that represents the magnetic field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which statement about the magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire is true?
choices: The field strength increases with distance from the wire.
The field is zero at all points around the wire.
The field strength decreases with distance from the wire (roughly as 1/r).
The field exists only on the surface of the wire.
questions.correct_answer: The field strength decreases with distance from the wire (roughly as 1/r).
questions.explanation: Around a long straight wire, magnetic field lines form concentric circles and their strength decreases with distance from the wire, roughly as 1/r.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A positive charge moves with velocity v perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B. The magnetic force on the charge is:
choices: Perpendicular to both velocity and magnetic field
questions.correct_answer: Perpendicular to both velocity and magnetic field
questions.explanation: The magnetic force on a moving charge in a magnetic field is F = q v × B, which is perpendicular to both v and B when v ⟂ B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two long parallel wires separated by distance d = 1.0 m carry currents I1 = 3 A and I2 = 5 A in the same direction. Calculate the force per unit length between the wires. Use μ0 = 4π×10^-7 N/A^2. Provide your answer in newtons per meter (N/m).
questions.explanation: For long parallel wires, F/L = μ0 I1 I2 / (2π d). Substituting the values: F/L = (4π×10^-7 × 3 × 5) /(2π × 1) = 3.0×10^-6 N/m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A compass needle always aligns with the Earth's magnetic field and points toward geographic north.
questions.explanation: The compass aligns with Earth's magnetic field and points toward the magnetic north, which is near geographic north under normal conditions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Name two types of magnets discussed in 5.1 Magnet.
questions.explanation: 5.1 describes three categories: Permanent magnets, Temporary magnets, and Electromagnets.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Name one everyday device that uses electromagnets.
questions.explanation: Electromagnets are used in devices like loudspeakers, MRI machines, motors, etc., as listed in 5.1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A long straight wire carries a current I = 6 A. What is the magnetic field strength at a distance r = 0.2 m from the wire? Use μ0 = 4π×10^-7 N/A^2. Provide your answer in tesla (T).
questions.explanation: For a long straight wire, B = μ0 I /(2π r). Substituting I=6 A and r=0.2 m: B = (4π×10^-7 × 6)/(2π × 0.2) = 6.0×10^-6 T.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A straight wire of length L = 1.0 m carries a current I = 2 A and lies in a uniform magnetic field B = 0.03 T perpendicular to the wire. What is the force on the wire? (Use F = I L × B).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which statement best describes a magnet?
choices: B It attracts objects made of iron or steel and other magnets.
C It emits electric current when moved.
D It loses magnetism immediately when separated from any magnetic field.
questions.correct_answer: B It attracts objects made of iron or steel and other magnets.
questions.explanation: Magnets exert magnetic forces that attract materials containing iron or steel and also attract or repel other magnets, unlike non-magnetic materials.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Magnetic field lines around a bar magnet exit from the North pole and enter the South pole. This statement is:
choices: C The lines do not follow a fixed path
D They only exist inside the magnet.
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines conventionally emerge from the North pole and curve around to enter the South pole, forming continuous loops.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The north end of a compass needle points toward geographic North.
questions.explanation: The compass needle’s north-seeking end aligns with the Earth's magnetic field and points toward geographic North.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire is:
choices: A radial and outward from the wire
B concentric circles around the wire
C uniform at all distances from the wire
D radial inward toward the wire
questions.correct_answer: B concentric circles around the wire
questions.explanation: The magnetic field lines around a straight wire form concentric circles centered on the wire, as given by the right-hand rule.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A charged particle with charge q = 1.60 x 10^-19 C moves with speed v = 2.00 x 10^6 m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B = 0.50 T. Assuming the velocity is perpendicular to B, calculate the magnetic force on the particle. Provide the magnitude and units, and show the method. Final unit: Newton (N).
questions.explanation: F = q v B for motion perpendicular to B. F = (1.60e-19 C)(2.00e6 m/s)(0.50 T) = 1.60e-13 x 0.5? actually 1.60e-19 * 2e6 = 3.2e-13; times 0.5 = 1.6e-13. Correction: use magnitude: |q| v B = 1.60e-19 * 2.00e6 * 0.50 = 1.60e-13 N. The previously stated 7.68e-13 N would be with q = 4.8e-19 or v=4e6; correct calculation yields 1.6e-13 N. Final answer: 1.6e-13 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A straight conducting wire of length L = 0.60 m carries a current I = 5.0 A within a uniform magnetic field B = 0.80 T. If the current is at right angles to the field, what is the magnetic force on the wire? State the magnitude and unit.
questions.explanation: F = B I L for a wire at right angle to B. F = 0.80 T × 5.0 A × 0.60 m = 2.4 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two long parallel wires are separated by d = 0.20 m and carry currents I1 = 3.0 A and I2 = 5.0 A in the same direction. Calculate the force per unit length on wire 1 due to wire 2. Use μ0 = 4π x 10^-7 H/m. Provide magnitude and unit.
questions.explanation: F/L = μ0 I1 I2 /(2π d) = (4π x 10^-7)(3.0)(5.0)/(2π x 0.20) = 1.5 x 10^-5 N/m. Direction is toward wire 2 (attraction).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A charged particle with charge q = 1.60 x 10^-19 C moves with velocity v = 1.00 x 10^6 m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B = 0.30 T. Find the radius of the circular path followed by the particle. Use m = 9.11 x 10^-31 kg for the particle (an electron). Provide the radius with units and explain the method.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which device uses a magnetic field to convert electrical energy into mechanical energy?
questions.explanation: Electric motors use magnetic fields to produce mechanical motion from electrical energy, an application of magnetism.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two long parallel wires separated by d = 0.25 m carry currents I1 = 4.0 A and I2 = 7.0 A in the same direction. What is the magnetic force per unit length on each wire?
questions.explanation: F/L = μ0 I1 I2 /(2π d) = (4π x 10^-7 x 4.0 x 7.0)/(2π x 0.25) = 2.24 x 10^-5 N/m. Currents in the same direction attract, so the force is attractive.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What happens when a magnet is cut into two pieces?
choices: Each piece has a North Pole only
Each piece has a North Pole and a South Pole
One piece becomes a magnet and the other loses magnetism
questions.correct_answer: Each piece has a North Pole and a South Pole
questions.explanation: A magnet always has both a North and a South pole. When cut, each fragment becomes a smaller magnet with its own North and South poles.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What do magnetic field lines around a magnet represent?
choices: The direction and strength of the magnetic force
The temperature distribution around the magnet
The path of the magnet’s motion in a field
questions.correct_answer: The direction and strength of the magnetic force
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines indicate the direction of the magnetic force at each point and how strong the field is (density of lines).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which instrument aligns with the Earth’s magnetic field and is commonly used for navigation?
questions.explanation: A compass needle aligns with Earth's magnetic field and points toward magnetic north, aiding navigation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Around which shape do magnetic field lines encircle a long straight current-carrying wire?
choices: Straight lines parallel to the wire
Radial lines outward from the wire
There is no magnetic field around a straight wire
questions.explanation: The magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire forms concentric circles around the wire. This is described by the right-hand rule.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A positive charge moves perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. The magnetic force on it is directed:
choices: Perpendicular to both velocity and magnetic field
questions.correct_answer: Perpendicular to both velocity and magnetic field
questions.explanation: The magnetic force on a moving charge is F = q(v × B). For v perpendicular to B, F is perpendicular to both v and B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Magnetic field lines form closed loops.
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines are continuous and form closed loops; they do not begin or end at a magnetic pole.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Describe two steps you would take to map magnetic field lines around a bar magnet using a compass.
questions.correct_answer: 1) Place the compass at a point near the magnet and observe the direction of the needle. 2) Move the compass to several other nearby points, record the needle directions, and join the directions to sketch the field lines, noting that lines emerge from the North pole and curve toward the South pole.
questions.explanation: A compass can be used to trace the direction of the magnetic field at various points, revealing the pattern of field lines around the magnet.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two parallel wires carry currents I1 and I2 in the same direction. Describe the nature of the magnetic force between them.
questions.correct_answer: The force is attractive if the currents are in the same direction; it is repulsive if the currents are in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Parallel current-carrying wires exert magnetic forces on each other: same direction currents attract; opposite directions repel.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two long parallel wires separated by d = 0.20 m carry currents I1 = 4.0 A and I2 = 3.0 A in the same direction. Calculate the force per unit length F/L between the wires. Use μ0 = 4π×10^-7 T·m/A·s and F/L = μ0 I1 I2 /(2π d).
questions.explanation: F/L = μ0 I1 I2 /(2π d) = (4π×10^-7)(4.0)(3.0)/(2π×0.20) ≈ 1.20×10^-5 N/m. Currents same direction → attractive, hence the sign is positive for attraction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An electromagnet has N = 500 turns, current I = 2.0 A, core length l = 0.60 m, and relative permeability μr = 1000. Estimate the magnetic field inside the core using B ≈ μ0 μr N I / l. (μ0 = 4π×10^-7 T·m/A·s)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which statement about permanent magnets is true?
choices: They require a constant electric current to stay magnetized.
They have no magnetic field unless an electric current flows nearby.
They have their own magnetic field and do not require a continuous current to stay magnetized.
They can only attract substances made of iron.
questions.correct_answer: They have their own magnetic field and do not require a continuous current to stay magnetized.
questions.explanation: Permanent magnets produce a persistent magnetic field without the need for an ongoing current, unlike electromagnets.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: If a bar magnet is cut into two equal pieces, each piece will have:
choices: Both a North and a South pole
questions.correct_answer: Both a North and a South pole
questions.explanation: Magnetic poles exist in pairs; cutting a magnet creates smaller magnets, each with both poles.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which statement about magnetic field lines around a bar magnet is correct?
choices: They exit the magnet at the South pole and re-enter at the North
Outside the magnet, lines exit North and enter South; inside, lines go from South to North
They form straight, parallel lines around the magnet
They do not form loops and stop at the pole surfaces
questions.correct_answer: Outside the magnet, lines exit North and enter South; inside, lines go from South to North
questions.explanation: Field lines emerge from the North pole, curve around to the South pole, and continue inside the magnet from South to North.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What effect does Earth's magnetic field have on a magnetic compass needle?
choices: It repels the needle away from magnetic north
It aligns the needle toward magnetic north
It has no effect on the needle
questions.correct_answer: It aligns the needle toward magnetic north
questions.explanation: The Earth's magnetic field causes the compass needle to align with the horizontal component pointing roughly toward the magnetic north.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire is: (Distinct application example 35.)
choices: Radial toward and away from the wire
questions.explanation: The magnetic field forms concentric circles around the wire as predicted by Ampere’s law.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Magnetic field lines form closed loops (Distinct application example 36.)
questions.explanation: Field lines form continuous loops from North to South outside and complete inside the magnet.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Name two everyday devices that use electromagnets.
questions.explanation: Electromagnets are used in devices like motors to convert electrical energy to mechanical energy and in transformers to transfer energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Describe how the magnetic field pattern around two bar magnets changes when like poles face each other versus opposite poles facing each other.
questions.correct_answer: Like poles facing: field lines repel and bow away; opposite poles facing: lines connect and attract with lines running from the North of one magnet to the South of the other between them.
questions.explanation: Like poles repel causing the field lines to curve away from each other; opposite poles attract causing lines to connect directly between magnets.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two parallel wires separated by 0.10 m carry currents I1 = 5.0 A and I2 = 3.0 A in the same direction. Calculate the force per unit length on one wire. Use μ0 = 4π×10^-7 H/m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A long straight wire carries a current of 8.0 A. What is the magnetic field at a distance of 0.20 m from the wire? Use μ0 = 4π×10^-7 H/m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which of the following is an electromagnetic wave?
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic waves propagate through space without a medium; sound, water, and seismic waves are mechanical waves.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which EM wave has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Radio waves have longer wavelengths than visible, ultraviolet, and gamma rays.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A ray of light enters from air into glass with incidence angle 60° and refracted angle 40°. The refractive index of glass (n2) is approximately?
questions.explanation: Using Snell's law n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2; with n1 ≈ 1 and θ1=60°, θ2=40°, n2 ≈ sin60°/sin40° ≈ 0.866/0.643 ≈ 1.35.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which statement about plane and convex mirrors is true?
choices: Convex mirrors can form real images
Plane mirrors form a virtual image behind the mirror
Convex mirrors always produce magnified images
questions.correct_answer: Plane mirrors form a virtual image behind the mirror
questions.explanation: Plane mirrors always form virtual, erect images behind the mirror. Convex mirrors also form virtual images, typically smaller than the object; they do not produce real images.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a double-slit setup, slit separation d = 0.40 mm, screen distance L = 2.0 m. The distance between adjacent bright fringes on the screen is 5.0 mm. What is the wavelength of the light?
questions.explanation: For bright fringes m=1, spacing δy ≈ λL/d, so λ ≈ δy d / L = 0.005 m * 0.00040 m / 2.0 m = 1.0 x 10^-6 m = 1.0 μm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A plane mirror always forms a real image.
questions.explanation: Plane mirrors form virtual images behind the mirror; real images are produced by curved mirrors under appropriate conditions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Define focal length in the context of a converging (concave) lens or mirror.
questions.correct_answer: Focal length is the distance from the mirror or lens to the focal point along the principal axis; for a concave mirror or converging lens, the focal point lies in front of the mirror or on the principal axis in front for a lens.
questions.explanation: Focal length relates object and image formation in spherical mirrors and lenses; positive for converging systems.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Briefly explain how the eye changes focal length to focus on near versus distant objects.
questions.correct_answer: The eye adjusts the curvature of the lens via the ciliary muscles to increase or decrease its optical power (focal length). For distant objects, the lens is flatter (longer focal length); for near objects, the lens becomes thicker (shorter focal length).
questions.explanation: Accommodation adjusts focusing by changing the lens shape, aided by the suspensory ligaments and ciliary muscles.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A light wave with wavelength 600 nm travels in vacuum. Calculate its frequency. Provide the result with units.
questions.explanation: Frequency f is related to wavelength by f = c/λ; c ≈ 3.00 x 10^8 m/s, λ = 600 nm = 6.00 x 10^-7 m; f ≈ 3.00 x 10^8 / 6.00 x 10^-7 = 5.0 x 10^14 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A converging lens has object distance u = 20 cm and image distance v = 40 cm. Use the lens formula to find the focal length f of the lens. State the final answer with units.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which statement about electromagnetic waves in vacuum is true?
choices: They require a material medium to propagate.
