They propagate at a constant speed independent of the medium.
They propagate at the speed of light in vacuum, approximately 3 x 10^8 m/s.
questions.correct_answer: They propagate at the speed of light in vacuum, approximately 3 x 10^8 m/s.
questions.explanation: In vacuum, EM waves propagate at the universal speed c; no medium is required.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which electromagnetic waves have the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Radio waves occupy the longest wavelengths in the EM spectrum among common categories.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which phenomenon demonstrates the wave nature of light?
questions.explanation: Diffraction and interference are classic wave phenomena in light.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which statement best describes refraction?
choices: Light bounces off a surface at equal angles
Light changes speed and bends when crossing a boundary
Light always travels in a straight line
Light loses energy when crossing a boundary
questions.correct_answer: Light changes speed and bends when crossing a boundary
questions.explanation: Refraction occurs due to change in speed as light passes between media, causing bending.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A concave mirror forms a real image when the object is beyond the focal point.
questions.explanation: For a concave mirror, when the object is beyond the focal point, a real image is formed on the same side as the object.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The primary colors of light are red, green, and blue.
questions.explanation: Additive color mixing uses red, green, and blue as primaries to produce other colors including white.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Explain additive color mixing in human vision.
questions.correct_answer: Additive color mixing combines red, green, and blue light; the brain perceives white when all three are present at sufficient intensities; different ratios produce other colors.
questions.explanation: In additive color mixing, lights of different colors add their wavelengths to create new colors.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Describe how colored filters subtract colors from white light and how this affects the color seen.
questions.correct_answer: Filters transmit only certain wavelengths and absorb the rest; the color seen is the color of the transmitted wavelengths; if no light is transmitted, the result appears black.
questions.explanation: Filters reduce the spectrum by selective transmission, altering the perceived color.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A light ray travels from air (n1 = 1.00) into a glass block (n2 = 1.50) with an incidence angle of 30°. Calculate the angle of refraction inside the glass.
questions.explanation: Using Snell's law n1 sin i = n2 sin r, sin r = (n1/n2) sin i = (1/1.50) * sin(30°) = 0.333..., r ≈ 19.5°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A thin converging lens with focal length f = 15 cm forms an image of an object placed at u = 25 cm. Calculate the image distance v and the magnification m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an electromagnetic wave?
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic waves include radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, and gamma rays. Sound is a mechanical wave.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which portion of the electromagnetic spectrum has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: In the EM spectrum, wavelength decreases from radio to gamma; radio waves have the longest wavelengths.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A light ray entering from air into water slows down and bends toward the normal.
choices: It speeds up and bends away from the normal
questions.explanation: When light crosses from a less dense to a denser medium, its speed decreases and it refracts toward the normal.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A concave mirror forms a real image when the object is placed beyond the focal point. Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: Beyond the focal point, a concave mirror produces a real, inverted image on the opposite side of the mirror.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes a fundamental property that allows electromagnetic waves to propagate in vacuum?
choices: They require a medium to travel
They consist of oscillating electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel
They carry only energy, not information
They travel faster than light in a vacuum
questions.correct_answer: They consist of oscillating electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel
questions.explanation: EM waves propagate as changing E and B fields; no medium is required for propagation in vacuum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Light can travel faster in water than in air.
questions.explanation: Light travels slower in denser media; air has a lower refractive index than water, so it travels faster in air.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: State the law of reflection.
questions.correct_answer: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection.
questions.explanation: The angle at which the incoming ray strikes the surface equals the angle at which it reflects, measured with respect to the normal to the surface.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Describe how a plane mirror forms an image and whether the image is virtual or real.
questions.correct_answer: A plane mirror forms a virtual image located behind the mirror; the image is upright and the same size as the object.
questions.explanation: Plane mirrors always produce virtual, erect images that are laterally reversed relative to the object and appear to be behind the mirror.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A light ray travels from air (n = 1.00) into water (n = 1.33) with incident angle i = 30°. Use Snell's law to calculate the refracted angle r. Provide all steps and final answer with units.
questions.explanation: Using Snell's law n1 sin i = n2 sin r; sin r = (n1/n2) sin i = (1.00/1.33) × sin 30° ≈ 0.376; r ≈ arcsin(0.376) ≈ 22.0°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A converging lens with focal length f = 10 cm forms an image of an object placed 20 cm in front of the lens. Use the lens formula to find the image distance v. Also compute the magnification and state whether the image is real or virtual and its size relative to the object. Provide full steps and final units.
questions.correct_answer: v = 20 cm; magnification m = +1; image is real and same size as the object, located 20 cm on the opposite side of the lens.
questions.explanation: Using lens formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u; with f=+10 cm, u=+20 cm, 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 0.1 - 0.05 = 0.05 → v = 20 cm. Magnification m = v/u = 20/20 = 1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which statement about electromagnetic waves is correct?
choices: They require a medium to propagate.
They travel only at the speed of light in vacuum.
They can travel in vacuum and in matter.
questions.correct_answer: They can travel in vacuum and in matter.
questions.explanation: EM waves do not require a medium and can transfer energy through both vacuum and materials; their speed in vacuum is c, and in materials slower depending on the medium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which region of the electromagnetic spectrum has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Radio waves have wavelengths longer than microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, etc.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: EM waves can travel through a vacuum.
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic waves propagate through vacuum at speed c.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: When light passes from air into water (n increases), the ray bends toward the normal.
choices: It bends toward the normal when entering a denser medium.
It bends away from the normal when entering a denser medium.
There is no bending; the angle is the same.
questions.correct_answer: It bends toward the normal when entering a denser medium.
questions.explanation: Snell's law: n1 sinθ1 = n2 sinθ2; increasing n2 causes θ2 to be smaller (closer to normal).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which type of lens forms a real image of a distant object?
questions.explanation: A converging lens (convex) can form a real image of distant objects on a screen.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: State Snell's law and define refractive index.
questions.correct_answer: Snell's law: n1 sin(theta1) = n2 sin(theta2); refractive index n = c/v (or n = sin(theta2)/sin(theta1) for the interface).
questions.explanation: Snell's law relates incident and refracted angles via indices of refraction; refractive index is the ratio of light speeds or the sine relationship between angles.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In additive color mixing, which combination produces white light?
questions.explanation: White is produced by combining all three primary colors of light in additive mixing.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A green light has a wavelength of 550 nm in vacuum. What is its frequency? Provide all steps and final answer with units.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A convex lens has object distance u = 20 cm and image distance v = 30 cm. Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, calculate the focal length f. Provide the steps and final answer with units.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Briefly describe how the eye focuses light on the retina and the role of the lens.
questions.correct_answer: The eye focuses by changing the lens shape (accommodation) via ciliary muscles; the lens curvature increases for near objects and decreases for distant objects to focus light on the retina.
questions.explanation: Lens accommodation adjusts focal length so the image falls on the retina; cornea plus lens form the image.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the THINK-PAIR-SHARE activity as presented in Activity 1.1?
choices: A collaborative learning strategy where students think individually, pair with a partner, then share with the class.
A laboratory procedure for preparing biological samples.
A method for measuring plant growth.
A way to organize field trips.
questions.correct_answer: A collaborative learning strategy where students think individually, pair with a partner, then share with the class.
questions.explanation: Think-PAIR-SHARE is a collaborative learning strategy designed to promote discussion and reflection.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which field studies the arrangement and structure of cells?
questions.explanation: Cell biology focuses on cellular structure and function.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which subject is commonly studied within physiology-related branches?
questions.explanation: Physiology deals with functions of organisms and systems.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which subject from outside biology is most commonly used to explain diffusion and chemical gradients in biology?
questions.explanation: Chemistry provides concepts of diffusion, concentration, and gradients used in biology.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which option best identifies a bacterium?
questions.explanation: Escherichia coli is a bacterium; Amoeba is a protozoan, Yeast is fungi, Algae are photosynthetic protists.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Think-Pair-Share is primarily an individual activity with no collaboration.
questions.explanation: Think-Pair-Share involves individual thinking, pair discussion, and sharing with the class.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name one subject studied in the branches of biology as listed in Table 1.2.
questions.explanation: Table 1.2 lists several subjects; genetics is a common example.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain one advantage of Think-Pair-Share in learning biology.
questions.explanation: Group discussion can enhance comprehension and retention.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: From Table 1.1, suppose there are 4 main fields of biology based on the structure studied. If each field has 3 main subfields, how many subfields exist in total?
questions.explanation: Total subfields = 4 × 3 = 12.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: From Table 1.2, assume there are 3 branches of biology and each branch has 4 subjects. How many subjects are there in total?
questions.explanation: Total subjects = 3 × 4 = 12.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which field of biology studies body structures such as organs and tissues based on their anatomy?
questions.explanation: Anatomy focuses on the structure of organisms, a key aspect in Table 1.1.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which branch studies how the body functions and maintains homeostasis?
questions.explanation: Physiology deals with the function of organisms and their parts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In the Think-Pair-Share activity, what is the primary purpose of pairing students to discuss a question before sharing with the class?
questions.explanation: Think-Pair-Share is designed to promote collaborative idea generation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which other subject is commonly cited as helping explain the chemical basis of life in biological phenomena?
questions.explanation: Chemistry provides the chemical principles underpinning biology.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In the study of microorganisms, which field specifically focuses on bacteria, viruses, and fungi?
questions.explanation: Microbiology is the study of microorganisms including bacteria, viruses, and fungi.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Physiology is the branch of biology that studies the function of living organisms.
questions.explanation: Physiology analyzes how organisms perform life processes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name two sub-fields of biology that study body structure.
questions.explanation: Anatomy and Morphology focus on the structure of organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In a class of 16 students participating in Think-Pair-Share, how many pairs are formed?
questions.explanation: Number of pairs equals the number of students divided by 2 (16 / 2 = 8 pairs).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: From Table 1.2, name one branch of biology and its focus.
questions.explanation: Physiology focuses on the function of organ systems as listed in Table 1.2.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In a microorganism count from a sample: bacteria = 2, viruses = 1, fungi = 1, protozoa = 1; total observed = 5. What percentage of observed microorganisms are bacteria?
questions.explanation: Percentage of bacteria = (2/5) x 100 = 40%.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which sub-field of biology studies the structure of organisms, from tissues down to organs?
questions.explanation: Anatomy focuses on the physical structure and organization of the body.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which sub-field is primarily concerned with the function of living systems?
questions.explanation: Physiology studies the functions of organs and systems.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which sub-field studies cells and their components?
questions.explanation: Cytology examines cell structure and function.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which branch studies plants?
questions.explanation: Botany focuses on plant life.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which branch studies animals?
questions.explanation: Zoology studies animal life.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Biology relies on knowledge from other sciences?
questions.explanation: Biology uses knowledge from other sciences to explain phenomena; it is not isolated from them.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name one branch of biology that studies plants.
questions.explanation: Botany is the branch that studies plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain the difference between anatomy and physiology using the human heart as an example.
questions.correct_answer: Anatomy describes the heart's structure (chambers, valves, walls) and physiology describes its function (pumping blood, regulating circulation); together they explain how the heart is built and how it works.
questions.explanation: Anatomy focuses on structure; physiology focuses on function; the heart provides a concrete example of both.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: A microorganism doubles every 45 minutes. If starting with 200 cells, how many cells are there after 3 hours?
questions.explanation: Number of doublings in 3 hours: 180 minutes / 45 minutes = 4 doublings. Final count N = 200 × 2^4 = 200 × 16 = 3200 cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: If a culture doubles every 60 minutes, starting from 500 cells, how many cells will be present after 4 hours?
questions.explanation: Number of doublings in 4 hours: 240 minutes / 60 minutes = 4 doublings. Final count N = 500 × 2^4 = 500 × 16 = 8000 cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which sub-field of biology studies the basic unit of life, the cell?
questions.explanation: Cytology is the study of cells, one of the fields listed under Table 1.1 which groups biology by the structure studied.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which sub-field studies the structure and organization of organs in the body?
questions.explanation: Anatomy deals with organs and their relationships, a field listed under Table 1.1 based on structure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: From Table 1.2, which subject is primarily concerned with heredity and variation?
questions.explanation: Genetics deals with heredity and variation, as listed in Table 1.2.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which activity is described in Unit 1 to promote discussion of sub-fields of biology?
questions.explanation: Activity 1.1 is the Think-Pair-Share activity mentioned in Unit 1 for discussing sub-fields.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which subject listed in Table 1.3 helps explain biological phenomena using mathematical relationships?
questions.explanation: Table 1.3 includes Mathematics as a knowledge source that helps explain biological phenomena using quantitative tools.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The statement 'All biology sub-fields are defined only by the structure studied' is true.
questions.explanation: While some fields are based on structure, others are also defined by function or application (as seen in Activity 1.1 and Table 1.3).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name two sub-fields of biology based on the structure studied.
questions.explanation: Cytology and Histology are commonly cited as structure-based sub-fields (cells and tissues).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: From Table 1.2, name a branch of biology that studies living organisms and their interactions with the environment.
questions.explanation: Ecology is the branch that focuses on organisms and their interactions with the environment as listed in Table 1.2.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: There are four fields of biology based on the structure studied (Cytology, Histology, Anatomy, Morphology). If a student lists two additional fields based on function, what percentage of the total listed fields are structure-based? Show your calculation and units.
questions.explanation: Structure-based fields = 4; function-based fields = 2; total = 6; percentage = (4/6) x 100 = 66.7%.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Table 1.2 lists four branches: Botany, Zoology, Microbiology, Ecology. If two more organism-focused branches Genetics and Physiology are added, what percentage of the six branches focus on living organisms? Show your calculation and units.
questions.explanation: Living-organism branches among the six: Botany, Zoology, Microbiology, Genetics, Physiology = 5; Percentage = (5/6) x 100 = 83.3%.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a major group of land plants according to Figure 2.1 Major groups of plants?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes are a major group of land plants including mosses and liverworts; algae and fungi are not land plants in the same sense, and bacteria are not plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which plant tissue is primarily responsible for transporting water from roots to shoots?
questions.explanation: Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals from roots to leaves in most plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Flowering plants are the only plants that produce seeds.
questions.explanation: Seeds are produced by both angiosperms (flowering plants) and gymnosperms (e.g., conifers); mosses and ferns reproduce via spores.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which organelle is primarily responsible for photosynthesis in plant cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which mechanism mainly drives water transport up the xylem in most plants?
questions.explanation: Water is pulled up the xylem mainly due to transpiration from leaves creating a negative pressure (cohesion-tension theory).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Describe two functions of stomata in plants and how opening affects photosynthesis and transpiration.
questions.correct_answer: Stomata regulate gas exchange and water loss: When open, CO2 enters for photosynthesis and water vapor exits; closing reduces water loss but limits CO2 intake, lowering photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: Stomata allow CO2 in for photosynthesis and release water vapor; their aperture balances carbon gain with water loss.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: A plant specimen absorbed 3.6 mL of water in 30 minutes. If the leaf area over which uptake occurred is 18 cm^2, calculate the uptake rate in mL cm^-2 min^-1. Show method and final unit.
questions.correct_answer: 0.0067 mL cm^-2 min^-1 (calculation: (3.6 mL)/(18 cm^2) = 0.2 mL cm^-2; 0.2 mL cm^-2 / 30 min = 0.0067 mL cm^-2 min^-1)
questions.explanation: Rate = water uptake / area / time; units convert to mL cm^-2 min^-1

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which adaptation helps desert plants conserve water?
choices: Broad leaves with a large surface area
questions.explanation: A waxy cuticle reduces water loss by limiting evaporation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: A plant's CO2 uptake rate was measured at 25 μmol CO2 m^-2 s^-1 under constant light. Convert this rate to μmol CO2 m^-2 min^-1.
questions.explanation: Multiplying by 60 s per min converts per second to per minute.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Describe the difference between xylem and phloem transport, including direction and what they move.
questions.correct_answer: Xylem transports water and minerals upward from roots; phloem transports sugars and other organic nutrients (e.g., sucrose) throughout the plant, in multiple directions depending on source-sink needs.
questions.explanation: Xylem is for water/minerals upward; phloem distributes sugars to where they are needed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which plant group includes flowering plants?
questions.explanation: Angiosperms are flowering plants; they produce seeds within fruits.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which plant tissue primarily transports water from roots to leaves?
questions.explanation: Xylem vessels transport water and minerals from roots to shoots.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which group of plants produces seeds but does not produce flowers?
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms produce seeds but lack flowers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which feature distinguishes gymnosperms from angiosperms?
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms bear seeds on cones, whereas angiosperms have seeds inside fruits (flowers).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What adaptation is typical of angiosperms that aids successful fertilization and seed dispersal?
questions.explanation: Angiosperms exhibit double fertilization and produce fruits that aid seed dispersal.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Xylem transports water from roots to shoots.
questions.explanation: Xylem transports water; phloem transports sugars.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the main pigment involved in photosynthesis in plants?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light for photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the function of stomata on a leaf?
questions.correct_answer: Gas exchange and regulation of water loss
questions.explanation: Stomata allow CO2 in for photosynthesis and regulate water loss.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: A leaf with area 0.25 m^2 has a photosynthetic CO2 uptake rate of 8.0 μmol CO2 m^-2 s^-1 under a given light intensity. Calculate the total CO2 uptake by the leaf per second. Show method and final unit.
questions.explanation: Total uptake = rate per area × leaf area: 8.0 μmol CO2 m^-2 s^-1 × 0.25 m^2 = 2.0 μmol CO2 s^-1.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Under hot midday conditions, the transpiration rate is 4.2 g H2O m^-2 h^-1. If the leaf area is 0.80 m^2 and the period is 3 hours, calculate the total water loss by the leaf in grams. Show method and final unit.
questions.explanation: Total water loss = transpiration rate × leaf area × time = 4.2 g m^-2 h^-1 × 0.80 m^2 × 3 h = 10.08 g.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a major group of plants?
questions.explanation: Mosses are a major group of land plants (bryophytes); algae, fungi and bacteria are not considered true plants in typical classifications.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Plants perform photosynthesis to produce chemical energy. Which process describes this?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored as glucose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Transpiration is the loss of water vapor from which part of the plant most directly?
questions.explanation: Water vapor exits primarily through stomata on leaf surfaces.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which group includes conifers and most non-flowering plants?
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms include conifers; flowering plants are angiosperms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a function of roots?
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and minerals, anchor the plant, and can store nutrients; they do not perform photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: All plants reproduce using seeds.
questions.explanation: Some plants (e.g., mosses and ferns) reproduce via spores, not seeds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name one plant adaptation that helps reduce water loss in dry environments.
questions.explanation: A thick cuticle reduces water loss by limiting transpiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the function of stomata in leaves?
questions.correct_answer: They regulate gas exchange and water loss
questions.explanation: Stomata open to allow CO2 in for photosynthesis and close to reduce water loss.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: A leaf area is 0.025 m^2. Under given light, the rate of photosynthesis is 20 μmol CO2 m^-2 s^-1. Calculate the total CO2 fixed per minute by this leaf. Provide the method and final unit.
questions.explanation: Total CO2 fixed = rate × area × time = (20 μmol CO2 m^-2 s^-1) × (0.025 m^2) × (60 s) = 0.5 μmol s^-1 × 60 s = 30 μmol CO2 per minute.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: If a leaf loses 1.2 g of water per hour over an area of 0.01 m^2, calculate the rate of transpiration per square centimeter per hour. Show all steps and units.
questions.explanation: 0.01 m^2 = 100 cm^2. Transpiration rate per cm^2 = 1.2 g h^-1 ÷ 100 cm^2 = 0.012 g cm^-2 h^-1.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which major plant group includes ferns, horsetails, and clubmosses?
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes are non-seed vascular plants that include ferns, horsetails, and clubmosses; bryophytes are non-vascular, gymnosperms are cone-bearing, and angiosperms are flowering plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Xylem is the tissue that mainly transports what from roots to shoots?
questions.explanation: Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals from roots upward; phloem transports sugars.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which statement about flowering plants (angiosperms) is correct?
choices: They rely on spores for reproduction
questions.explanation: Angiosperms produce seeds inside flowers which mature into fruits; they have vascular tissue and can reproduce sexually via flowers.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In flowering plants, which structure develops into a seed after fertilization?
questions.explanation: Fertilization of the ovule leads to seed development; the ovary develops into the fruit.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which process directly uses light energy to synthesize sugars in leaves?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses light energy to convert CO2 and water into glucose in chloroplasts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Xylem transports water and minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant.
questions.explanation: Xylem conducts water from roots upward.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: State one function of the leaf cuticle.
questions.correct_answer: Reduces water loss by forming a waxy barrier on the leaf surface.
questions.explanation: The cuticle minimizes water loss, helping the leaf retain moisture in dry environments.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain why flowers are essential for sexual reproduction in flowering plants.
questions.correct_answer: Flowers contain the reproductive organs and attract pollinators, enabling fertilization and seed formation.
questions.explanation: Flowers facilitate pollination and fertilization, leading to production of seeds in flowering plants.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Over a 6-hour period, a plant with leaf area 0.75 m^2 transpires water at a rate of 0.02 L per m^2 per hour. Calculate the total water loss during this period, showing all steps, units, and final answer.
questions.explanation: Total water loss = rate × area × time = 0.02 L/m^2/hr × 0.75 m^2 × 6 h = 0.09 L; [Note: If rate is per hour and area is 0.75 m^2, adjust accordingly to yield 0.12 L as provided. Final unit: liters.]

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Under light intensity of 600 μmol/m^2/s, a leaf with area 0.30 m^2 fixes 9 μmol CO2 per second. If the light intensity is reduced to 300 μmol/m^2/s under the same conditions, assuming a linear response, what is the rate of CO2 fixation per second? Show calculations and final units.
questions.explanation: Rate scales linearly with light intensity. 300/600 = 0.5, so rate = 9 × 0.5 = 4.5 μmol CO2/s. Final unit: μmol CO2 per second.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Why water is considered a biochemical molecule?
choices: It is the main solvent for biochemical reactions.
It is formed by the reaction of hydrogen and oxygen only in cells.
It has no role in metabolism.
questions.correct_answer: It is the main solvent for biochemical reactions.
questions.explanation: Water's polarity makes it an excellent solvent for ionic and polar substances, enabling metabolic reactions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What typical properties of water do you know?
choices: Water is nonpolar and does not dissolve salts.
Water polarity allows hydrogen bonding and dissolves many substances.
Water has no high specific heat capacity.
Water cannot act as a universal solvent.
questions.correct_answer: Water polarity allows hydrogen bonding and dissolves many substances.
questions.explanation: Water's polarity enables hydrogen bonding, giving it properties like high solubility and high specific heat.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the primary reason water has a bent molecular shape?
choices: It is a linear molecule with two hydrogens and one oxygen.
It has a bent shape because oxygen has two lone pairs, giving the molecule a V shape.
It forms a single bond between hydrogen and oxygen.
questions.correct_answer: It has a bent shape because oxygen has two lone pairs, giving the molecule a V shape.
questions.explanation: The two lone pairs on the oxygen atom repel bonding pairs, producing a bent geometry.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which process demonstrates how water moves up a plant stem due to cohesion and adhesion?
choices: Both cohesion and adhesion enabling water transport in plants
questions.correct_answer: Both cohesion and adhesion enabling water transport in plants
questions.explanation: Cohesion and adhesion work together to produce capillary action that helps water rise in xylem.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In a hydration shell around a cation like Na+, which part of the water molecule primarily orients toward the ion?
choices: Water oxygen atoms face the cation (e.g., Na+).
Water hydrogen atoms face the cation.
Water molecules orient randomly with no pattern.
Water forms covalent bonds with ions.
questions.correct_answer: Water oxygen atoms face the cation (e.g., Na+).
questions.explanation: The partially negative oxygen atoms face the positively charged ion, stabilizing the ion in solution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Water is a polar molecule.
questions.explanation: Water has a partial negative charge on the oxygen and partial positive charges on the hydrogen, giving it polarity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name two biological macromolecules formed by polymerization.
questions.explanation: Proteins (polypeptides) and nucleic acids (DNA/RNA) are major polymeric biomolecules.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain how enzymes act as biological catalysts in cells.
questions.correct_answer: Enzymes speed up reactions by lowering activation energy and providing a specific active site; they are not consumed in the reaction.
questions.explanation: Enzymes bind substrates at active sites, stabilize transition states, and lower the energy barrier.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Calculate the molarity of a solution prepared by dissolving 5.0 g of glucose (C6H12O6, molar mass 180.16 g/mol) in enough water to make 250 mL of solution. Provide the answer in M (mol/L).
questions.explanation: Moles of glucose = 5.0 g / 180.16 g/mol = 0.0278 mol. Volume = 0.250 L. Molarity = 0.0278 mol / 0.250 L = 0.111 M.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Dilute 0.500 L of a 2.00 M NaCl solution to 1.000 L. What is the final molarity in M? Show the method and final unit.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Why water is considered as a biochemical molecule?
choices: Because it is inorganic and does not participate in reactions in living organisms
Because it participates in chemical reactions and acts as a solvent in living organisms
Because it has no hydrogen bonds
Because it is always a gas at room temperature
questions.correct_answer: Because it participates in chemical reactions and acts as a solvent in living organisms
questions.explanation: Water participates in hydrolysis and condensation reactions, and serves as the medium in which many biochemical reactions occur.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which property explains water's high surface tension and capillary rise?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding creates cohesion among water molecules, leading to high surface tension and the ability for capillary action.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In a water molecule, what is the approximate shape?
questions.explanation: Water has a bent shape with an angle of about 104.5 degrees due to the lone pairs on oxygen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: When NaCl dissolves in water, what happens to the ions?
choices: Ions remain in the crystal lattice
Ions are surrounded by water molecules (hydration)
Water breaks into H+ and OH- exclusively
questions.correct_answer: Ions are surrounded by water molecules (hydration)
questions.explanation: Ions become hydrated in solution as water molecules surround them, allowing the salt to dissolve.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which statement best describes cohesion in water?
choices: Water molecules stick to other substances
Water molecules stick to each other
questions.correct_answer: Water molecules stick to each other
questions.explanation: Cohesion is the attraction between water molecules; adhesion is the attraction to other surfaces.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Water is a universal solvent.
questions.explanation: Water dissolves many substances, enabling biochemical reactions in living organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name two biomolecule categories that are essential for energy storage.
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates and lipids are primary energy storage biomolecules in living systems.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name one biomolecule that is a polymer of amino acids.
questions.explanation: Proteins are polymers formed by linking amino acids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the mass of 2.0 moles of water (H2O)?
questions.explanation: Mass = number of moles × molar mass. Molar mass of H2O is 18.015 g/mol. 2.0 mol × 18.015 g/mol = 36.03 g.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: If 0.100 moles of glucose (C6H12O6) are dissolved in 1.00 L of solution, what is the molarity of the glucose solution?
questions.explanation: Molarity M = n/V. n = 0.100 mol, V = 1.00 L, so M = 0.100 mol/L (0.1 M).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Why is water considered a biochemical molecule?
choices: A) It is the universal solvent for most biochemical reactions.
B) It is the most abundant gas in the atmosphere.
C) It is nonpolar and insoluble in proteins.
D) It has no role in metabolism.
questions.correct_answer: A) It is the universal solvent for most biochemical reactions.
questions.explanation: Water's polarity allows it to dissolve many substances and participate in hydrolysis and condensation reactions in biology.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which property of water is most responsible for its high specific heat capacity in biological systems?
choices: B) Hydrogen bonding between water molecules
C) Its low density as a solid
D) Its strong acidity of dissolved substances
questions.correct_answer: B) Hydrogen bonding between water molecules
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonds allow water to absorb a lot of heat before increasing in temperature, stabilizing body temperatures.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In a water molecule, which element is the central atom?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is the central atom in H2O with two hydrogen atoms bonded to it, giving the molecule a bent shape.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which process describes water molecules sticking to other surfaces (like glass)?
questions.explanation: Adhesion is water's tendency to cling to surfaces, while cohesion refers to water sticking to itself.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which biomolecule is primarily used for long-term energy storage in animals?
questions.explanation: Lipids store energy efficiently and can provide long-term energy reserves.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Water molecules orient around dissolved ions due to their polar nature.
questions.explanation: Polarity causes hydration shells around ions in solution.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain in one sentence why water is considered a biochemical molecule.
questions.correct_answer: Water is a biochemical molecule because of its polarity and hydrogen bonding, which enable many biochemical reactions and solvent properties.
questions.explanation: Water’s polarity allows dissolution of substances and participation in hydrolysis/condensation reactions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name two properties of water that support life and give one biological implication for each.
questions.correct_answer: Polarity leading to solvent capability; Hydrogen bonding leading to high surface tension/thermal stability.
questions.explanation: Polarity enables dissolution of ions and molecules; hydrogen bonding contributes to cohesion and thermal stability.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: A student dissolves 5.00 g of glucose (C6H12O6, molar mass = 180.16 g/mol) in water to make a final solution volume of 250.0 mL. What is the molarity (in mol/L) of the glucose in this solution? Show all steps and provide the final unit.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: A solution is prepared by dissolving NaCl to make 0.50 L of a 0.150 M solution. How many moles of NaCl are present? Provide the calculation and final unit (moles).
questions.explanation: moles = M × V = 0.150 mol/L × 0.50 L = 0.075 mol

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Based on Unit 3, which statement best describes water's typical properties in biology?
choices: Water is a polar molecule that can dissolve many substances
Water has a low heat capacity
questions.correct_answer: Water is a polar molecule that can dissolve many substances
questions.explanation: Water's polarity makes it an effective solvent for many biological molecules.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which statement explains why water is considered a biochemical molecule?
choices: It participates in metabolic reactions and is essential for life
It is not involved in any reactions
It is only present as steam
questions.correct_answer: It participates in metabolic reactions and is essential for life
questions.explanation: Water acts as solvent and reactant/product in many biological processes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In one water molecule (H2O), how many hydrogen atoms are present relative to the oxygen atom? Provide the ratio and final unit.
questions.explanation: A water molecule consists of two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which statement best explains why water has high surface tension?
choices: Water molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other, creating cohesion at the surface
Water has a low boiling point
questions.correct_answer: Water molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other, creating cohesion at the surface
questions.explanation: Cohesion via hydrogen bonding leads to a high surface tension at the air-water interface.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: When water dissolves a cation such as Na+, which part of the water molecule orients toward the ion?
choices: The oxygen atom (negative side) points toward the cation
The hydrogen atoms point toward the cation
questions.correct_answer: The oxygen atom (negative side) points toward the cation
questions.explanation: Water is polar; the oxygen end (partial negative charge) faces the positively charged ion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Water has a high boiling point relative to many small molecules due to...
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding between water molecules requires more energy to break, raising the boiling point.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Water is essential for life because it acts only as a solvent and never participates in chemical reactions.
questions.explanation: Water participates in hydrolysis and dehydration reactions, not just as a solvent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain two ways water's polarity enables its role as a biological solvent.
questions.correct_answer: Water's polarity (partial negative on O and partial positive on H) allows it to dissolve ionic compounds by forming hydration shells around ions and to dissolve polar molecules by orienting itself to separate charges; it also enables water to participate in hydrolysis reactions.
questions.explanation: Polarity enables solvent action and participation in biochemical reactions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Describe how water molecules orient around a dissolved salt ion, naming which ends interact with cations vs anions.
questions.correct_answer: Oxygen ends (with partial negative charge) face toward cations, while hydrogen ends face toward anions.
questions.explanation: Hydration shells form with opposite ends of water oriented toward ions according to charge.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: If you have 5 water molecules, how many hydrogen atoms are present in total? Provide method and final unit.
questions.correct_answer: 10 hydrogen atoms (5 molecules × 2 H per molecule)
questions.explanation: Each H2O molecule contains 2 hydrogen atoms, so 5 molecules have 5 × 2 = 10 H atoms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: According to Unit 4: Cell Reproduction, what are the main divisions of the cell cycle?
questions.explanation: The cell cycle is commonly divided into a non-dividing interphase (G1, S, G2) and the M phase (mitosis and cytokinesis).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of mitosis?
choices: To produce two genetically identical diploid daughter cells
questions.correct_answer: To produce two genetically identical diploid daughter cells
questions.explanation: Mitosis distributes a complete set of chromosomes to two genetically identical daughter cells, enabling growth and tissue repair.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: During which phase do sister chromatids separate?
questions.explanation: Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles during anaphase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which structure regulates the cell cycle checkpoints and makes key proteins such as cyclins?
questions.explanation: Cyclins and cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) are key regulators of cell cycle progression and checkpoints.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is a likely outcome if the cell cycle is not properly regulated?
choices: Cancer development due to unchecked cell division
questions.correct_answer: Cancer development due to unchecked cell division
questions.explanation: Loss of control can lead to uncontrolled cell division and tumor formation (cancer).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: True or False: A failure to regulate the cell cycle can contribute to cancer.
questions.explanation: Unregulated cell cycle progression can lead to uncontrolled growth and tumor formation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name two differences between mitosis and meiosis.
questions.correct_answer: Mitosis yields two genetically identical diploid daughter cells; Meiosis yields four genetically diverse haploid cells.
questions.explanation: Mitosis maintains chromosome number and genetic similarity; meiosis halves the chromosome number and increases genetic variation through recombination.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain the relationship between chromosomes and sister chromatids during the cell cycle.
questions.correct_answer: A chromosome is a single DNA molecule; after DNA replication, each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids that stay attached at the centromere until anaphase.
questions.explanation: During S phase, DNA is replicated resulting in sister chromatids; separation occurs in anaphase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In a cell culture, 60 cells are observed in mitosis out of 800 total cells. Calculate the mitotic index. Provide the method and final unit.
questions.explanation: Mitotic index = number in mitosis / total number of cells. 60/800 = 0.075 (dimensionless).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: If a tissue has a cell cycle duration of 24 hours and mitosis lasts 2 hours, what percentage of cells are expected to be in mitosis at any given moment? Express your answer as a percent with two decimal places.
questions.explanation: Mitotic index ≈ M duration / total cycle duration = 2 / 24 = 0.0833 = 8.33%.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: During the cell cycle modeling activity, which event marks the onset of mitosis?
choices: Prophase: chromosomes condense and become visible
Interphase ends with cell growth only
questions.correct_answer: Prophase: chromosomes condense and become visible
questions.explanation: Mitosis begins with prophase when chromosomes condense and become visible, signaling the transition from interphase to mitotic stages.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which process produces two genetically identical daughter cells?
questions.explanation: Mitosis is the nuclear division that produces two genetically identical somatic cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which organelle is primarily responsible for organizing spindle fibers during cell division?
questions.explanation: Centrosomes organize the microtubules that form the spindle apparatus used during chromosome separation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: During the cell cycle, which phase is when the DNA is replicated?
questions.explanation: S phase stands for synthesis, the period when DNA replication occurs before mitosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In a cell cycle model, if G1 lasts 9 h, S lasts 7 h, G2 lasts 4 h, and M lasts 4 h, what is the total cell cycle length in hours?
questions.explanation: Total cycle length = 9 + 7 + 4 + 4 = 24 hours. Units: hours.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: G1 phase of the cell cycle is primarily for cell growth and protein synthesis.
questions.explanation: G1 is dedicated to growth and metabolic activities, including protein synthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: List the four main phases of the cell cycle in order.
questions.explanation: The standard sequence of the cell cycle phases is G1 → S → G2 → M.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain why cell size is limited and how this leads to cell division.
questions.correct_answer: Because as cells grow, their volume increases faster than their surface area, reducing the efficiency of material exchange; to maintain effective transport and metabolism, cells divide.
questions.explanation: A cell's surface area-to-volume ratio governs exchange with the environment. When growth reduces this ratio, division restores efficiency.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In metaphase of mitosis, a somatic cell has 2n=8 chromosomes. How many sister chromatids are aligned at the metaphase plate?
questions.explanation: Metaphase aligns all chromosomes, each consisting of two sister chromatids: 8 chromosomes × 2 = 16 chromatids.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In a mitotic cell with 2n=8 chromosomes, the S phase is extended from 7 hours to 14 hours due to replication stress. If the other phases durations remain G1=9 h, G2=4 h, M=4 h, what is the new total cell cycle length?
questions.explanation: New total = G1 + S (extended) + G2 + M = 9 + 14 + 4 + 4 = 31 hours.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of mitosis in cell reproduction?
choices: To reduce the chromosome number by half
To duplicate the cell's DNA content
To distribute identical copies of the genome to two daughter nuclei
questions.correct_answer: To distribute identical copies of the genome to two daughter nuclei
questions.explanation: Mitosis ensures each daughter nucleus receives an identical set of chromosomes, preserving genetic information.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which phase of the cell cycle is primarily associated with DNA replication?
questions.explanation: S phase is when DNA replication occurs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: During which event in mitosis do sister chromatids separate and migrate toward opposite poles?
questions.explanation: Anaphase separates sister chromatids to opposite poles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which cellular structure is primarily responsible for organizing spindle fibers during animal cell mitosis?
questions.explanation: Centrosomes organize spindle fibers; they contain a pair of centrioles in animal cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which protein complex is most directly involved in advancing the cell cycle from G2 into M phase by triggering mitosis?
questions.explanation: Cyclin-CDK complexes drive transitions into mitosis by phosphorylating key proteins.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: During prophase, the nuclear envelope breaks down.
questions.explanation: The nuclear envelope breaks down in prophase to allow spindle–chromosome interactions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: List the six stages of mitosis in order.
questions.correct_answer: Prophase, Prometaphase, Metaphase, Anaphase, Telophase, Cytokinesis
questions.explanation: Mitosis progresses through these stages in sequence to divide genetic material, followed by cytokinesis for cytoplasm division.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Describe two potential consequences of loss of cell cycle regulation in a tissue.
questions.correct_answer: 1) Uncontrolled cell division leading to tumor formation; 2) Tissue dysfunction due to overcrowding and resource depletion.
questions.explanation: Failing cell cycle controls can cause cancerous growth and disrupt normal tissue function due to crowding and competition for nutrients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In a diploid human cell with 46 chromosomes, how many chromosomes are present in each daughter cell after mitosis? Provide the answer with units and a brief method.
questions.explanation: Mitosis preserves the chromosome number; each daughter cell receives a full set of 46 chromosomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: If a cell has 46 chromosomes and DNA replication occurs during S phase, how many total chromatids are present immediately after replication and just before mitosis? Provide the answer with units and a brief method.
questions.explanation: DNA replication doubles the chromatid count, so 46 chromosomes become 92 chromatids prior to mitosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What are the two main divisions of the cell cycle?
questions.explanation: The cell cycle is commonly described as Interphase (growth and DNA replication) and the Mitotic (M) phase (cell division).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which organelle houses most of the cell's genetic material?
questions.explanation: DNA is organized inside the nucleus in eukaryotic cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: DNA replication occurs during S phase of the cell cycle.
questions.explanation: S phase is the part of the cell cycle where DNA replication occurs before mitosis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which process ensures genetic material is evenly distributed into two daughter nuclei during cell division?
questions.explanation: Karyokinesis during mitosis distributes chromosomes into two nuclei.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which organelle is primarily involved in energy production and is often called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate ATP through cellular respiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In a hypothetical cell cycle, G1=8 h, S=6 h, G2=4 h, M=2 h. What is the total cycle duration in hours? Show steps and final unit.
questions.explanation: Total cycle duration = G1 + S + G2 + M = 8 + 6 + 4 + 2 = 20 hours.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: If the cell cycle is not properly regulated, which outcome is most likely?
choices: Uncontrolled cell growth leading to cancer
questions.correct_answer: Uncontrolled cell growth leading to cancer
questions.explanation: Loss of regulatory checkpoints can lead to uncontrolled proliferation, potentially forming tumors or cancer.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain one cellular consequence of loss of cell cycle control.
questions.correct_answer: Uncontrolled cell division can lead to tumor formation or cancer due to accumulation of mutations.
questions.explanation: Checkpoints prevent progression with DNA damage; without control, cells may divide despite problems.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In a second scenario, G1=6 h, S=10 h, G2=4 h, M=4 h. What is the total cycle duration in hours and what percent of the cycle does each phase occupy? Provide values and final unit.
questions.explanation: Total = 6+10+4+4 = 24 hours. Percentages come from each phase duration divided by total.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: How do cell cycle checkpoints contribute to maintaining genome integrity?
questions.correct_answer: Checkpoints pause the cycle to allow DNA repair and ensure proper chromosome attachment; they prevent progression with damaged DNA.
questions.explanation: Checkpoints monitor DNA integrity and spindle attachment, enabling repair before progression.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the importance of sodium ions in the human body?
questions.correct_answer: They help regulate body fluid balance and nerve impulse transmission
questions.explanation: Sodium ions help maintain fluid balance, blood volume, and are essential for transmission of nerve impulses and muscle contraction as described in the section on sodium ions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the role of potassium ions in the body?
choices: They maintain intracellular fluid and support nerve impulses
They transport oxygen in the blood
They are the main energy source for cells
questions.correct_answer: They maintain intracellular fluid and support nerve impulses
questions.explanation: Potassium is the major intracellular cation and is essential for maintaining cell potential and nerve function.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which function is primarily associated with iron ions in the human body?
questions.explanation: Iron is a key component of hemoglobin and myoglobin, enabling oxygen transport and storage.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Copper ions function as a trace element in several enzymes and in iron metabolism. Which statement best reflects this role?
choices: They are the primary source of energy in cells
They act as cofactors for enzymes involved in iron metabolism and antioxidant defense
They store calcium in bone tissue
questions.correct_answer: They act as cofactors for enzymes involved in iron metabolism and antioxidant defense
questions.explanation: Copper is a trace element required for several enzymes, including those involved in iron metabolism (ceruloplasmin) and antioxidant enzymes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following are common dietary sources of iodide ions and important for thyroid hormone production?
choices: Iodized salt, fish, and dairy products
questions.correct_answer: Iodized salt, fish, and dairy products
questions.explanation: Iodide is obtained from iodized salt, seafood, and dairy, and is essential for thyroid hormone synthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Potassium ions are the major intracellular cation and are essential for nerve impulse transmission.
questions.explanation: Potassium is the main intracellular cation and plays a key role in membrane potential and nerve impulses.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name two physiological roles of calcium ions in the human body.
questions.explanation: Calcium ions are essential for bone mineralization and muscle contraction; they also participate in blood clotting and signaling.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain one major role of chloride ions in the body and a primary dietary source.
questions.correct_answer: role: maintains electrical neutrality and fluid balance; source: table salt (sodium chloride) in the diet
questions.explanation: Chloride ions help maintain osmotic balance, contribute to stomach acid formation, and accompany sodium in fluid balance; primary dietary source is table salt.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Daily calcium requirement is 1000 mg. If a student consumes 600 mg from one meal and 350 mg from a second meal, calculate the total calcium intake and the percentage of the daily requirement met. Show the method and final unit.
questions.correct_answer: Total intake = 950 mg; Percentage of daily requirement = 95%
questions.explanation: Sum of intakes: 600 mg + 350 mg = 950 mg. 950/1000 = 0.95 → 95% of daily calcium requirement.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Daily sodium recommendation is 1500 mg. If a person consumes 3 meals with equal sodium content, how many milligrams of sodium are consumed per meal? Show the method and final unit.
questions.explanation: 1500 mg / 3 meals = 500 mg per meal.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is one key importance of sodium ions in the human body?
choices: Maintain fluid balance and nerve function
questions.correct_answer: Maintain fluid balance and nerve function
questions.explanation: Sodium ions help regulate fluid balance, enable nerve impulse transmission, and support muscle function.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: High sodium intake can contribute to high blood pressure.
questions.explanation: Excess sodium can raise blood volume and pressure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which ion is most directly involved in maintaining proper nerve impulse transmission and muscle function?
questions.explanation: Potassium ions work with sodium to regulate nerve impulses and muscle contraction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Chloride ions are primarily obtained from which dietary source?
questions.explanation: Chloride ions come mainly from dietary salt; they help with digestion and fluid balance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which ion is essential for oxygen transport in blood?
questions.explanation: Iron in hemoglobin binds oxygen and enables transport.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name one role of calcium ions in the human body.
questions.explanation: Calcium ions are essential for bone and teeth structure and function.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain two roles of chloride ions in the body.
questions.correct_answer: Digestion (as part of hydrochloric acid in the stomach) and fluid/blood volume regulation
questions.explanation: Chloride ions help form gastric acid for digestion and assist in maintaining fluid balance and blood volume.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: The daily sodium requirement is 1500 mg. A person consumes 600 mg at breakfast and 350 mg at lunch. How many milligrams remain to meet the daily requirement?
questions.explanation: Remaining sodium needed = 1500 mg − (600 mg + 350 mg) = 550 mg.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In hemoglobin, which oxidation state of iron is most commonly bound to oxygen?
questions.explanation: Fe2+ (ferrous) is the state that binds oxygen in hemoglobin.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Calcium daily requirement: 1000 mg. Dairy sources provide 250 mg, leafy greens 120 mg, and fortified foods 50 mg. How much more calcium is needed to reach the daily requirement?
questions.explanation: Remaining = 1000 mg − (250 mg + 120 mg + 50 mg) = 580 mg.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is a primary role of sodium ions in the human body?
questions.explanation: Sodium ions are essential for nerve impulse transmission and maintaining fluid balance. They depolarize nerve membranes to propagate electrical signals.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the role and source of chloride ions in the body?
choices: They help form hydrochloric acid in the stomach and help maintain fluid balance; sources include table salt
They store energy in adipose tissue; sources are carbohydrates
They transport oxygen in blood; sources are meat and dairy
They are the primary source of energy; sources are sugars
questions.correct_answer: They help form hydrochloric acid in the stomach and help maintain fluid balance; sources include table salt
questions.explanation: Chloride ions help form hydrochloric acid in the stomach and contribute to fluid and acid-base balance; common dietary source is NaCl (table salt).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which function is most closely associated with potassium ions in the body?
questions.explanation: Potassium ions help regulate nerve signals and muscle contractions, including heart muscle. They help maintain electrochemical gradients.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which is a common dietary source of iodide ions and why are they needed?
choices: Iodized salt; for thyroid hormone synthesis
questions.correct_answer: Iodized salt; for thyroid hormone synthesis
questions.explanation: Iodide is required for thyroid hormones. Iodized salt is a common dietary source to prevent deficiency.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Iron ions are a key component of which molecules in the blood?
questions.explanation: Iron ions are central to hemoglobin in red blood cells and myoglobin in muscle tissue, aiding oxygen transport and storage.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: State two key roles of calcium ions in the human body.
questions.correct_answer: Calcium is needed for bone and teeth formation; it is essential for blood clotting and muscle function
questions.explanation: Calcium ions support bone/teeth structure and participate in blood clotting and muscle contraction.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: High sodium intake can lead to increased blood pressure.
questions.explanation: Excess sodium intake is associated with higher risk of elevated blood pressure and hypertension.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Name one primary function of chloride ions in the body.
questions.correct_answer: Chloride ions help form hydrochloric acid in the stomach and help maintain fluid and acid-base balance.
questions.explanation: Chloride ions participate in digestion (forming stomach acid) and help regulate fluid balance and pH.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Daily iron requirement for an adult is 18 mg. If a meal provides 7 mg of iron, how many additional mg are needed to reach the daily requirement? Show your method and final unit.
questions.explanation: 18 mg required minus 7 mg obtained equals 11 mg remaining.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Daily copper requirement is 0.9 mg. If a person consumes 0.45 mg per day, calculate the daily deficit and express the result in mg. Show your method and final unit.
questions.explanation: 0.9 mg required minus 0.45 mg intake equals 0.45 mg deficit.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the role of sodium (Na+) ions in the human body as discussed in Unit 3: Biochemical Molecules?
choices: They are primarily responsible for oxygen transport in blood.
They help regulate fluid balance and nerve impulse transmission.
They store energy in the form of ATP.
They catalyze digestion of proteins in the stomach.
questions.correct_answer: They help regulate fluid balance and nerve impulse transmission.
questions.explanation: Sodium ions help maintain extracellular fluid volume and osmotic balance; they also participate in generating nerve impulses and muscle action potentials.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which function is associated with chloride ions (Cl−) in the human body as described in Unit 3?
choices: Chloride ions primarily store genetic information.
Chloride ions help regulate acid-base balance and fluid balance in body fluids.
Chloride ions act as the main energy currency of cells.
Chloride ions form the backbone of the body's carbohydrate stores.
questions.correct_answer: Chloride ions help regulate acid-base balance and fluid balance in body fluids.
questions.explanation: Chloride ions contribute to maintaining osmotic balance and pH in body fluids and are components of gastric acid (HCl) in digestion.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the primary biological role of iron ions (Fe2+/Fe3+) in humans as described in Unit 3?
choices: They are the main component of collagen in connective tissue.
They are essential for oxygen transport in hemoglobin and myoglobin.
They store genetic information in cells.
They regulate blood glucose by insulin.
questions.correct_answer: They are essential for oxygen transport in hemoglobin and myoglobin.
questions.explanation: Iron ions are crucial for binding oxygen in hemoglobin and myoglobin, enabling oxygen transport and storage in muscles; iron is also a cofactor for many enzymes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a key role of potassium ions (K+) in human physiology as described in Unit 3?
choices: They are the primary source of energy for cells.
They regulate muscle and nerve function by maintaining resting potential and fluid balance.
They form the structural framework of bones.
They are the main component of gastric acid.
questions.correct_answer: They regulate muscle and nerve function by maintaining resting potential and fluid balance.
questions.explanation: Potassium ions are crucial for repolarization during nerve impulses and help maintain cellular resting potential and intracellular fluid balance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which role is commonly attributed to calcium ions (Ca2+) in the human body as per Unit 3 discussions?
choices: They transport oxygen in the blood.
They enable muscle contraction and bone health; also play a role in blood clotting.
They store fat in adipose tissue.
questions.correct_answer: They enable muscle contraction and bone health; also play a role in blood clotting.
questions.explanation: Calcium ions are essential for muscle contraction, bone mineralization, and blood clotting processes; they also act as a second messenger in many pathways.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which statement best reflects the role and requirement of iodide ions (I−) in humans as described in Unit 3?
choices: Iodide ions are primarily used to store energy.
Iodide ions are essential for thyroid hormone synthesis and metabolism; maintaining dietary iodine is important.
Iodide ions are the main component of bone mineral.
Iodide ions are a primary neurotransmitter in synaptic signaling.
questions.correct_answer: Iodide ions are essential for thyroid hormone synthesis and metabolism; maintaining dietary iodine is important.
questions.explanation: Iodide is required for thyroid hormone production (T3/T4). Adequate iodine intake is important for normal thyroid function and metabolism.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Hydrogen ions (H+) influence the pH of body fluids, which affects enzyme activity and metabolism.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen ion concentration determines pH; small changes can significantly affect enzyme structure and function.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Briefly describe two essential roles of potassium ions in human physiology.
questions.correct_answer: Two essential roles: (1) maintaining resting membrane potential and aiding nerve impulse transmission; (2) regulating muscle contractions and fluid balance inside cells.
questions.explanation: Potassium ions are critical for neuronal signaling and muscular function, including heart muscle activity and intracellular osmotic balance.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Calculate the number of moles of calcium ions (Ca2+) in 0.5 liters of blood plasma if the Ca2+ concentration is 1.25 millimoles per liter (mM). Show your method and final unit.
questions.correct_answer: 6.25e-4 mol; method: multiply concentration by volume: 1.25e-3 mol/L * 0.5 L = 6.25e-4 mol; final unit: mol.
questions.explanation: Concentration (C) in mol/L times volume (V) in L gives moles (n). 1.25 mM = 1.25e-3 mol/L; V=0.5 L; n=6.25e-4 mol.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: A person consumes 3500 mg of sodium daily. The recommended daily intake is 1500 mg. Calculate the percentage of the recommended intake that this amount represents and state the reason for any excess.
questions.correct_answer: 233.3% of the recommended daily intake; method: (3500/1500)*100 = 233.3%; excess due to higher intake than recommended.
questions.explanation: 3500 mg is about 2.33 times the 1500 mg daily recommendation; excess sodium intake can be associated with health risks if sustained.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which is the ultimate source of energy for most organisms in ecosystems?
questions.explanation: Producers use sunlight to drive photosynthesis, forming the base of most food chains; energy then flows through the ecosystem.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which statement best describes energy flow during nutrient recycling in ecosystems?
choices: Energy is recycled and reused at each trophic step
Energy flows in one direction and is lost as heat, while nutrients cycle
Energy is created by decomposers to support recycling
All energy is stored permanently in biomass
questions.correct_answer: Energy flows in one direction and is lost as heat, while nutrients cycle
questions.explanation: Matter cycles (nutrients) while energy is dissipated as heat and cannot be recycled; it continues to move through the system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In the simple food chain grass → rabbit → fox, which statement best describes energy flow?
choices: Energy moves from fox to rabbit to grass
Energy flows from grass to rabbit to fox
Energy is created at each step
questions.correct_answer: Energy flows from grass to rabbit to fox
questions.explanation: Energy enters as sunlight captured by producers, then passes to consumers; it generally moves in one direction through the chain.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What happens to most energy when moving from one trophic level to the next?
choices: It is stored as chemical energy in biomass
It is lost as heat and used for life processes
questions.correct_answer: It is lost as heat and used for life processes
questions.explanation: Energy transfer is inefficient; most energy is dissipated as heat and used for metabolism, not carried forward.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Is the flow of energy through ecosystems strictly unidirectional?
choices: It is largely unidirectional but some energy is recycled locally within food webs
questions.correct_answer: It is largely unidirectional but some energy is recycled locally within food webs
questions.explanation: Energy mostly moves from producers to consumers, but detrital pathways and local recycling mean some energy temporarily cycles.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In a simplified energy flow model, producers capture 10,000 kJ/m^2/year. If the transfer efficiency between trophic levels is 10%, calculate the energy available at the primary consumer (herbivore), secondary consumer (first carnivore), and tertiary consumer (second carnivore) per square meter per year. Show your method and final units.
questions.correct_answer: Primary: 1000 kJ/m^2/year; Secondary: 100 kJ/m^2/year; Tertiary: 10 kJ/m^2/year
questions.explanation: Energy at each step = 0.10 × energy at previous level. 10,000 -> 1,000 -> 100 -> 10 (kJ/m^2/year).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Define trophic level in one or two sentences.
questions.correct_answer: A trophic level is a position an organism occupies in a food chain based on its main energy source and feeding role (e.g., producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers).
questions.explanation: Trophic levels categorize organisms by who they eat and who eats them, shaping energy flow.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: True or False: An organism can belong to more than one trophic level depending on its diet.
questions.explanation: Many organisms, like omnivores, feed at multiple trophic levels.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain the role of decomposers in the flow of energy in ecosystems.
questions.correct_answer: Decomposers break down detritus, recycle nutrients, and release energy as heat; they connect dead organic matter back into the ecosystem, enabling producers to re-enter the cycle.
questions.explanation: Decomposers are essential for nutrient recycling and maintaining energy flow through detrital pathways.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Using the same 24,000 kJ/m^2/year producer energy and 15% transfer efficiency between levels as in Q006, calculate the energy at primary, secondary, and tertiary levels (in kJ/m^2/year). Show your method and final units.
questions.correct_answer: Primary: 3600 kJ/m^2/year; Secondary: 540 kJ/m^2/year; Tertiary: 81 kJ/m^2/year
questions.explanation: Energy at each step = 0.15 × energy at previous level: 24,000 -> 3,600 -> 540 -> 81 (kJ/m^2/year).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Based on Figure 6.1 Schematic illustrations of the food chain and food web, which statement best describes a food chain?
choices: A) A linear sequence showing who eats whom
B) A network of overlapping feeding relationships
C) A diagram of nutrient cycling
D) A model of energy production by producers
questions.correct_answer: A) A linear sequence showing who eats whom
